jobs.title: Head of People & Organizational Effectiveness
jobs.excerpt: SEEKING. COMHead of People & Organizational Effectiveness Organization Design | Talent Selection | Team Effectiveness | Incentive Design | People Science Location: Remote, USCompany: Seeking.
jobs.description:
SEEKING.COM

Head of People & Organizational Effectiveness

Organization Design | Talent Selection | Team Effectiveness | Incentive Design | People Science

Location: Remote, US

Company: Seeking.com, STNDRDS, and Standards.com (combined US operating organization)

Reports to: Co-CEOs

Type: Full-Time, Exempt

Compensation: $175,000 to $225,000 base

The Question You Will Spend Your Time Answering

Why do some groups of talented people accomplish extraordinary things together, while other groups of equally talented people become slow, political, or frustrated? And how do we deliberately build the first kind?

If you have spent a meaningful part of your career thinking about that question, often when nobody was paying you to, keep reading.

About Us

Seeking.com is the world's largest premium dating platform, founded by an MIT alumnus and headquartered in Las Vegas. STNDRDS is our consumer media brand; Standards.com is our independent news publication. Together we are a combined US operating organization built on one premise: we exist to create value for the people we serve, not to extract it from them.

We are 50 to 60 people, split between our Las Vegas office and remote roles across the country, and we intend to stay small by design. We grow through leverage per person, not headcount. That makes how our people are selected, organized, and work together the single biggest determinant of what we can accomplish.

The Opportunity

You own the design and effectiveness of the human operating system of the company: what people and structure we need, how we select them, how we organize, develop, and reward them, and how they work together. You are not here to administer HR programs. You are here to make the organization, and every person in it, more effective.

The core question you carry every day:

Do we have the right people, organized the right way, operating under the right conditions and incentives, to accomplish what we are asking the company to accomplish?

When the answer is no, you diagnose before you prescribe. Is it the person, the manager, the structure, the incentives, the team composition, unclear ownership, decision rights, information flow, missing capability, or something nobody else has noticed? Then you design the smallest intervention that fixes the real cause, and you measure whether it worked.

Three ideas shape how we work. The Value Creator System: people earn gain share based on demonstrated repeatable value. The Certainty Framework: design work to create the conditions for eustress (voluntary striving toward something you care about) and remove structural sources of distress. The 10x Operating Principle: growth comes through leverage per person, not added headcount.

What You Will Own

You own the architecture of each area below. Payroll, benefits administration, and onboarding and offboarding logistics are run by our Director of Business Operations. You design the systems; that team helps run them.

1. Organizational Design and Diagnosis

Shape roles, teams, reporting lines, decision rights, and operating models around our strategy. Find overlaps, gaps, unnecessary layers, and structures built for yesterday. Be the company's organizational doctor: the person the Co-CEOs call when something involving people does not make sense. The org chart is an output of your thinking, not the starting point.

2. Talent Architecture, Recruiting, and Selection

The goal is capability per employee, not headcount. Before a role opens, ask whether AI, redesign, clearer ownership, or developing someone already here would solve the problem better. Own recruiting strategy, critical and leadership hiring, succession, and retention of high performers. Build selection methods that predict who will perform here, not who interviews well, and track quality of hire at six and twelve months to learn what actually predicts success. Shape an employer brand that attracts people energized by high standards and lets everyone else self-select out.

3. Individual and Team Effectiveness

Most of us, leadership included, can become dramatically more effective at the fundamentals: organizing work and information, focus, prioritization, problem-solving, decisions, and communicating ideas simply. Diagnose the habits limiting output and build simple interventions people actually use. Understand why some combinations of people multiply each other and others create friction. Coach the Co-CEOs on their own operating habits when relevant. That is part of the job, not a boundary.

4. Management, Performance, and Feedback

Managers amplify or suppress everyone around them. Own manager selection, development, delegation, 1:1 quality, and manager evaluation. Replace annual reviews and stack rankings with continuous, lightweight feedback close to the work. Every person should be able to answer: What is expected of me? How is my performance measured? What happens when I create exceptional value? What happens when I repeatedly do not perform? When someone struggles, determine whether it is a person, manager, role, structure, or incentive problem.

5. Communication Systems and Norms of Excellence

Design how we give feedback, disagree, raise bad news, present information, run meetings, and choose between synchronous and asynchronous work, including across our office and remote teams. Reset the norms so excellence is the polite behavior: it is impolite to sit in a meeting you are not adding to, and impolite to hold back a concern to avoid friction. Observe whether behavior actually changes, and adapt when it does not.

6. Planning and Operating Systems (with Program Management)

Program Management owns the executive planning process and operating cadence. You own its human effectiveness: whether priorities and OKRs actually land throughout the organization, whether people can connect their work to them, how teams plan their week, and whether reporting improves decisions or just creates more work.

7. Compensation, Incentives, and Gain Share

Own the architecture and behavioral design of pay: salary philosophy and bands, bonus structures, promotion criteria, and the gain share model behind the Value Creator System. Partner with the Co-CEOs and Finance on the economics. Keep asking what behavior each incentive will actually produce, and watch for gaming, internal competition, free riding, and short-term thinking. Build systems where people understand how creating more value for the company creates more value for them.

8. Employee Lifecycle and a Lean People Team

Design the lifecycle around what matters: how fast a new hire can create value independently, which people we cannot afford to lose and why, and what each departure teaches us about selection, management, or role design. Own career paths and the Associates Program for early-career talent. Build a small team (for example recruiting and learning specialists) as the work requires, with the same rigor you expect from every hiring manager.

Who You Might Be

There is no single acceptable career path. You might be a People leader whose real obsession has always been how organizations work, an organizational effectiveness or development leader, an applied organizational psychologist, an organization-design consultant ready to operate, or a founder or executive adviser. We care far more about how you think than about your title, your degree, or how many years you have held a particular job. What we need to see:

  • A track record of diagnosing difficult human or organizational problems and showing what changed because of your intervention
  • Experience redesigning structures, roles, decision rights, or operating models
  • Evidence you have improved individual, manager, or team effectiveness, not just delivered training
  • You have done this work from the inside at least once and lived with the results, not only as an outside adviser
  • Real thinking about incentives and motivation: team versus individual rewards, intrinsic versus extrinsic drive, unintended consequences
  • Comfort telling the Co-CEOs something they may not want to hear
  • Active use of AI in your own work and a view on how it should change the way teams are designed

Graduate training in industrial-organizational psychology, organizational behavior, or organization design is a plus. Like every senior leader here, you will set quarterly OKRs with leading and lagging measures and work in Confluence, Jira, and Monday.

How We Hire for This Role

We will not rely on polished interviews. We want to see how you think, so the process is transparent and mostly hands-on:

  1. A conversation about what you have studied. What you have spent years trying to understand about people and organizations.
  2. A diagnostic case. An anonymized real situation from our company. We will ask what you see and why, not what you would do.
  3. Observing a team. You review a leadership meeting (live or as a transcript) and tell us what the people in the room probably missed.
  4. Designing the intervention. What you would do next, how you would test it, and what could go wrong.

What Success Looks Like in Twelve Months

  • Our structure matches our strategy, and ownership and decision rights are clear
  • Managers measurably raise the performance of the people around them
  • Our selection process gets better at identifying extraordinary people, and we can prove it
  • Our incentives reward the behavior that creates the most value
  • Problems are caught early and diagnosed correctly instead of recurring
  • Meetings and communication take less time and produce better decisions
  • The Co-CEOs understand the organization, and themselves, better than before you arrived

Compensation

$175,000 to $225,000 base, based on demonstrated capability, plus gain share tied to demonstrated repeatable value, so exceptional impact produces total compensation well above base. We care about mission, and we believe incentives matter. Part of your job is helping us align the two. Benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k), flexible PTO, and a fully remote environment.

jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

COO / CEO-in-Training – Trustbridge Design & Manufacturing (South-East Asia)

Build the Next Platform for Global Manufacturing

Location: South-EastAsia ( South-East Asia, or East Asia preferred)
Reports to: Founder, Vulcury Venture Studio
Company: Trustbridge Design & Manufacturing

The Opportunity

Trustbridge Design & Manufacturing is building a platform for the global manufacturing economy.

Companies developing new products often struggle to identify the right manufacturing partners, while highly capable suppliers lack consistent access to qualified opportunities.

Trustbridge connects these two sides of the market.

The company combines:

  • Engineering design services that help companies move products from concept to production
  • A curated global network of manufacturing suppliers
  • Software tools designed to improve how product companies identify and engage manufacturing partners

The business is already operating, generating revenue, and profitable, and is now entering a phase focused on scaling operations and building the platform to power global growth.

Asia will be a critical region in this expansion, given its central role in global manufacturing supply chains.

Why This Role Exists

Trustbridge is seeking a COO / CEO-in-Training (South-East Asia) to work directly with the founder to expand and scale operations across South East Asia, and ultimately lead the region as CEO.

This role is designed for someone transitioning from advisor or senior operator into a full company-building leadership role, with ownership of regional P&L and strategic direction.

The individual will help establish Trustbridge’s presence across Asia, build supplier networks, and scale both service and technology offerings.

The Venture Studio Advantage

Trustbridge is incubated within Vulcury, a venture studio that builds and scales companies across technology, manufacturing, and financial services.

Vulcury provides shared infrastructure including:

  • Strategic research and market analysis
  • Marketing and growth capabilities
  • Operational and financial systems
  • Technical development resources
  • Access to advisors, investors, and industry partners

This allows Trustbridge leadership to focus on execution and scaling without building every function from scratch.

The Role

The COO / CEO-in-Training (South-East Asia) will lead two core areas:

Engineering & Design Services (Asia Expansion)
  • Build and scale regional engineering and design-for-manufacturing capabilities
  • Develop relationships with product companies across Asia
  • Support companies in bringing products from concept to production

Manufacturing Supplier Platform (Asia Network)
  • Build and expand a high-quality supplier network across key Asian manufacturing hubs
  • Contribute to the development of Trustbridge’s sourcing and supplier platform
  • Ensure strong alignment between platform capabilities and regional market needs

Key Responsibilities

Business Leadership

  • Define and execute Trustbridge’s Asia growth strategy
  • Build and lead the regional operations team
  • Establish scalable systems and processes

Platform Development

  • Help shape the supplier platform roadmap with regional insights
  • Work closely with technical teams to ensure product-market fit in Asia

Commercial Strategy

  • Drive customer acquisition across startups, product companies, and enterprises
  • Build strategic relationships with manufacturers and engineering partners

Organizational Development

  • Recruit and develop the regional leadership team
  • Build operational infrastructure for long-term growth
  • Prepare the region for scale and potential capital deployment

Compensation

This is a co-founder level opportunity.

Compensation includes:

  • Competitive base salary
  • Meaningful equity participation in Trustbridge
  • Performance-based incentives tied to regional and global growth

What Success Looks Like

Over the next several years, the successful candidate will:

  • Establish Trustbridge as a leading manufacturing partner in Asia
  • Build a strong and reliable supplier network across key markets (India, Vietnam, China, etc.)
  • Launch and scale the supplier platform in the region
  • Drive significant revenue growth from Asia operations

This role will naturally evolve into CEO – Asia, with full leadership responsibility for the region.


Requirements

Mandatory

  • MBA or equivalent strategic leadership experience
  • 10+ years in manufacturing, supply chain, engineering services, or industrial sectors
  • Strong operational and strategic leadership capabilities
  • Proven ability to build and lead teams
  • Entrepreneurial mindset

Highly Preferred

  • Background in management consulting (McKinsey, Bain, BCG, Deloitte, Strategy&)
  • Experience in South-East Asian manufacturing ecosystems
  • Experience with supply chain platforms or manufacturing tech
  • Experience working with product companies or engineering teams
  • Experience scaling early-stage ventures or business units

Because we build most features in Tarteel to work offline, the kind of challenges you will get to solve will push the limits of your skillset and expose you to challenges you haven’t previously encountered.   • Proactively identify and drive changes as needed across all product areas

Opportunity at a Glance

Forensic PhD Contributing faculty members primary responsibility will be to chair and/or serve as second members on doctoral dissertation committees as methodologists and/or content experts. Infrequently and based on student enrollment, and when applicable, Contributing Faculty may be invited to instruct content courses or to instruct research methodology courses, they are credentialed to teach. Participation in Mentor Training will be provided and required.
Contributing faculty members serve in a part-time capacity to educate Walden University Students by effectively and proficiently using online technology and resources so that knowledge, information, feedback, and critique are imparted to and shared with students in thoughtful, carefully formulated, well written, and timely communications. This is accomplished in an environment that is respectful of student, the Faculty Member, Walden University, and the discipline in which the Faculty Member is involved. Faculty Members are expected to adhere to all Walden University Faculty expectations, which are clearly set forth to the Faculty Member at the start of his/her employment with the University.
Responsibilities

  • Training: All new Faculty Members receive specific training from Walden University in the techniques teaching, use of an electronic learning platform, specifics of the policies, procedures and degree programs of the School or College in which they are going to teach, socialization into the Walden University culture, assessment of academic integrity of student work (including use of www.turnitin.com), and research supervision of theses and dissertations.
  • Course Teaching: Faculty Members are assigned a course, which is taught using the eCollege platform, and are responsible for interacting with students within this platform. Discussion Boards for classrooms are open 24 hours per day, 7 days per week. Although postings to the classroom may be done at any time of day, they must be completed in a timely manner in accordance with the Faculty Handbook or other criteria established by Walden University. Per the faculty handbook, responses to student questions must be posted within 48 hours. Faculty Members are required to verify the accuracy of student postings and submissions and to provide feedback and grades to students through Blackboard.
  • Availability: Walden expects faculty to be reasonably accessible to students. Faculty members are expected to be available to students outside the course discussion board and in addition to providing substantive feedback on assignments and postings. Faculty members will publish their availability to students through course syllabi, instructor information in the classroom, and/or other appropriate documents. The university suggests regular and predictable availability, such as online office hours or regular online chats.
  • Residencies: Faculty Members may be required to attend Residencies held domestically or internationally, (Part-time faculty may, but are not required to attend), where they will teach intensives and colloquia, and facilitate school and university-wide discussions.
  • Performs other duties as assigned
  • Complies with all policies and standards
  • PH.D in Forensic Psychology or a related field from an accredited institution required,
  • Forensic experience at the doctoral level preferred
  • Proof of serving on doctoral committees for 1 year (Preferably Chair of the committee)
  • Evidence of continuing scholarly or creative work within the past 5 years. Proficient in APA 7th edition
  • Strong research methodology background in quantitative, qualitative, and/or mixed methods in research (preference given to quantitative)
  • Excellent leadership, communication, team, and human relation skills.
  • At least 1,000 hours of direct forensic experienceover five years, or completion of a 2,000-hour formal postdoctoral fellowship in forensic psychology.

Technology Requirements:

  • Contributing faculty provide their own laptops and are expected to use the Walden University Learning Management System and the Microsoft 365 tools with their assigned Walden email addresses in their Walden activities. Walden University provides a Walden e-mail account and access to the learning platform, password-protected faculty sections of the website, university and college cloud services, and other faculty communications tools.

Walden University, an Adtalem Global Education institution, supports a diverse community of adult learners from across the U.S. and other countries, who seek to achieve their academic goals and make positive, lasting social change in their professions and communities. Are you interested in a career in Publishing? Does history never cease to amaze you? Are you a keen cook or an avid gardener?

If any, or all, of these things sound like you, and you would love to spend two weeks (9th - 20th November 2026) with us, then The DK Experience, our remote programme, might be the perfect match for you!

Who are we?

We’re DK (Dorling Kindersley), the biggest publisher of illustrated non-fiction in the world. We make books covering everything: travel, gardening, cooking, history, children's stories… you name it, we’ve probably got a book on it!

We’re looking for creative and passionate candidates to join us on the DK Experience, a paid two week work placement within one of our departments.

As much as we’d like to, high demand means we’re unable to offer everyone a place and we’ll be in contact to let you know if you have been randomly selected this time. We will not contact the unsuccessful candidates however if we don’t have a place for you on this occasion, please do keep trying. If you are successful you will hear from us by 15 October 2026.

Where are you from?

The programme requires no degree or previous publishing experience and aims to open the doors of our industry to participants from underrepresented regions, communities and backgrounds.

Publishing is traditionally very London-centric and people from London or the Home Counties (Buckinghamshire, Surrey, Berkshire, Essex, Hertfordshire, Kent, Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire, Hampshire, Oxfordshire, Sussex) or who are based in these regions, have traditionally been advantaged in gaining access to the industry.

This programme is instead for anyone originally from, or currently living, in Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland and parts of England outside London and the Home Counties. Please do not apply if you are currently living in, or originally from, London or the Home Counties (If you are from London, we do work closely with LDN and they may have programmes which might be more suitable for you. You can find out more about the LDN Publishing Apprenticeship here.)

Who are you?

You need to be above 18 years old to apply. You’ll also come from an experience or background that is currently underrepresented in publishing. This could include, but is not limited to, coming from a socio-economically marginalised background, being of Black, Asian or minority ethnic heritage, having a disabled and/or neurodiverse experience or living with a long-term health condition, or belonging to an LGBTQ+ community.

Please note, this programme is not aimed at candidates who already hold a Masters in Publishing.

What will you be doing?

This exciting opportunity will be completely remote. All you need is a computer, wifi connection, the right to work in the UK and to be able to commit to two weeks’ full-time work.

We’ll be taking you behind the scenes of our publishing house and introducing you to all the different areas of the industry. While you will be placed in a creative department, you’ll also have the opportunity to learn about all the other areas of our company.

You’ll attend meetings, try your hand at a variety of editing or designing tasks and get involved in a fun group project with other people on the placement. And along with this engaging creative experience, you’ll be paid the National Minimum Wage.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Serve as Product Owner and senior business analyst for the Salesforce platform (Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Communications Cloud/Vlocity, CPQ etc.), owning the platform roadmap, backlog, and release calendar.
  • Transform game-changing ideas that differentiate our company into clear designs, epics, and user stories that we can implement through technology.
  • Own and prioritize the Salesforce product backlog; write and refine user stories and acceptance criteria and define “definition of done” in partnership with development and QA teams.
  • Assist in the definition of project scope, requirements, and objectives across the Salesforce ecosystem, involving all relevant stakeholders and ensuring technical feasibility.
  • Coordinate internal resources and third parties/vendors, including Salesforce implementation and AppExchange partners, to document issue statements, business requirements, and Return on Investment (ROI).
  • Facilitate workshops or work sessions with to translate an initiative’s high-level concept into key design criteria.
  • Diagram and redesign cross-functional customer journeys and business processes spanning lead-to-order, service delivery introducing feasible processes implemented with people and Salesforce.
  • Author business and functional requirements, user stories, and integration specifications that clarify business rules, features, and other critical information for Salesforce enhancements.
  • Design integration and process improvements between Salesforce, billing, dispatch/field service management, workforce management, and adjacent enterprise systems to reduce manual workarounds and improve data accuracy.
  • Define test plan criteria and execute or oversee UAT/SIT against sandbox and production-like environments to evaluate whether documented requirements are sufficiently met before release.
  • Identify friction points, automation opportunities, and AI-enabled enhancements across self-service, contact center, and field service touchpoints, maintaining a prioritized continuous-improvement backlog.
  • Own and oversee functional documentation, configuration standards, and platform governance over time as a responsible steward of Salesforce processes and system workflows.
  • Monitor project progress and platform health by tracking activities, resolving problems, publishing progress reports, and advocating action against CX metrics (CSAT, NPS, FCR, time-to-resolution) and platform adoption metrics.
  • Partner with peers within Hotwire to streamline processes, drive end-to-end process improvements and efficiencies, and provide overall support to cross-functional teams.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, design, information technology, or a related field.
  • Minimum of five (5) years’ experience as a Product Owner, Senior Business Analyst, Platform Owner, Architect, or Consultant in operations, or customer experience functions.
  • Hands-on experience administering or configuring the Salesforce platform (Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Communications Cloud/Velocity, CPQ).
  • Experience in reporting and analysis, CX metrics (CSAT, NPS, FCR), and ROI analysis.
  • Knowledge of quality management technique and process improvement (Six Sigma): both in statistical analysis and in qualitative interviewing
  • Experience designing Journey Maps or other depictions of customer experience diagrams and documentation
  • Experience designing processes that were implemented as a software-enabled solutions such as customer-facing web experiences or internal employee toolsets/workflow
  • A strong understanding of the dynamic role of CX
  • Knowledge of cable and telecommunications products and services
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook)
  • Must embrace company principles and demonstrate understanding of concierge culture

jobs.title: Senior Early Career Recruiter
jobs.excerpt: About AbridgeAbridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare.
jobs.description:
About Abridge

Abridge was founded in 2018 with the mission of powering deeper understanding in healthcare. Our AI-powered platform was purpose-built for medical conversations, improving clinical documentation efficiencies while enabling clinicians to focus on what matters most—their patients.

Our enterprise-grade technology transforms patient-clinician conversations into structured clinical notes in real-time, with deep EMR integrations. Powered by Linked Evidence and our purpose-built, auditable AI, we are the only company that maps AI-generated summaries to ground truth, helping providers quickly trust and verify the output. As pioneers in generative AI for healthcare, we are setting the industry standards for the responsible deployment of AI across health systems.

We are a growing team of practicing MDs, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to empower people and make care make more sense. We have offices located in the Mission District in San Francisco, the SoHo neighborhood of New York, and East Liberty in Pittsburgh.

The Role

Early talent is one of the highest-leverage investments we can make in Abridge's future. We are looking for an Early Career Recruiter to help us identify and hire exceptional emerging talent with the ability, drive, and mission alignment to build meaningful careers here.

We want to create an early talent program that reaches broadly and assesses people for their potential, not only their pedigree. That includes exceptional candidates from leading universities as well as community colleges, bootcamps, apprenticeships, career transitions, and other paths.

You will partner closely with our Early Talent Program Manager and engineering leaders to build this capability from the ground up. You will own recruiting for interns and early career talent, primarily across software engineering, while helping us expand into other functions over time.

This is an opportunity for someone who loves recruiting, exercises strong judgment, and is energized by building a program—not simply inheriting one.

This role is based in our San Francisco office and requires being in the office three days per week.

What You’ll Do

  • Own end-to-end intern and early career recruiting, initially focused on software engineering

  • Partner with our Early Talent Program Manager to build and execute a differentiated hiring strategy

  • Find exceptional candidates across universities, technical communities, bootcamps, apprenticeships, and other talent channels including event strategies

  • Work with engineering leaders to define exceptional potential and build a rigorous, consistent evaluation process

  • Deliver a candidate experience that reflects how we operate at Abridge: demanding, caring, and mission-driven

  • Use pipeline data and hiring outcomes to continually improve our approach

  • Build the systems and partnerships needed to scale the program

  • Support other critical technical roles outside peak early talent cycles

What You’ll Bring

  • Experience recruiting software engineers, ideally including interns or early career talent

  • A track record of finding strong candidates through a range of sourcing channels

  • Enough technical fluency to evaluate engineering profiles and partner credibly with hiring managers

  • Strong judgment for recognizing potential, learning velocity, and motivation beyond traditional credentials

  • A builder's mindset and comfort creating structure in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment

  • High ownership, urgency, and care for the candidate experience

  • Genuine connection to Abridge's mission and excitement about helping emerging talent begin their careers here

Bonus Points If…

  • You have built or scaled an early talent program

  • You have recruited across both technical and non-technical early career roles

  • You have developed partnerships with bootcamps, apprenticeships, community colleges, or other alternative talent communities

This is a hybrid role requiring a minimum of 3 days per week in our San Francisco office, with flexibility for remote work on other days.

Why Work at Abridge?

At Abridge, we’re transforming healthcare delivery experiences with generative AI, enabling clinicians and patients to connect in deeper, more meaningful ways. Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month.

Joining Abridge means stepping into a fast-paced, high-growth startup where your contributions truly make a difference. Our culture requires extreme ownership—every employee has the ability to (and is expected to) make an impact on our customers and our business.

Beyond individual impact, you will have the opportunity to work alongside a team of curious, high-achieving people in a supportive environment where success is shared, growth is constant, and feedback fuels progress. At Abridge, it’s not just what we do—it’s how we do it. Every decision is rooted in empathy, always prioritizing the needs of clinicians and patients.

We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. Whether it's flexible work hours, an inclusive culture, or ongoing learning opportunities, we are here to help you thrive and do the best work of your life.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact alongside passionate people who care deeply about what they do, Abridge is the place for you.

How we take care of Abridgers:

  • Generous Time Off: 14 paid holidays, flexible PTO for salaried employees, and accrued time off for hourly employees

  • Comprehensive Health Plans: Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage for all full-time employees and their families.

  • Generous HSA Contribution: If you choose a High Deductible Health Plan, Abridge makes monthly contributions to your HSA.

  • Paid Parental Leave: Generous paid parental leave for all full-time employees.

  • Family Forming Benefits: Resources and financial support to help you build your family.

  • 401(k) Matching: Contribution matching to help invest in your future.

  • Personal Device Allowance: Tax free funds for personal device usage.

  • Pre-tax Benefits: Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Commuter Benefits.

  • Lifestyle Wallet: Monthly contributions for fitness, professional development, coworking, and more.

  • Mental Health Support: Dedicated access to therapy and coaching to help you reach your goals.

  • Sabbatical Leave: Paid Sabbatical Leave after 5 years of employment.

  • Compensation and Equity: Competitive compensation and equity grants for full time employees.

  • ... and much more!

Equal Opportunity Employer

Abridge is an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants equally without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or disability.

We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the interview process. Once you submit your application, we'll follow up with details on how to request an accommodation for interviewing, completing any assessments, or otherwise participating in the selection process.

Staying safe - Protect yourself from recruitment fraud

We are aware of individuals and entities fraudulently representing themselves as Abridge recruiters and/or hiring managers. Abridge will never ask for financial information or payment, or for personal information such as bank account number or social security number during the job application or interview process. Any emails from the Abridge recruiting team will come from an @abridge.com email address. You can learn more about how to protect yourself from these types of fraud by referring to this article. Please exercise caution and cease communications if something feels suspicious about your interactions.

Compensation Range: $155K - $175K

Senior ProductArchitect for Supply Chain Management HSO Studio

Location: Remote

Role overview

The (Lead) Product Architect will provide product architecture leadership across our Advanced Supply Chain Management (ASCM) bundle of products for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Built specifically for manufacturers and wholesale distributors, ASCM empowers organizations to streamline operations, improve fulfillment flexibility, and elevate the customer experience in a complex, omnichannel world. ASCM includes the following products, all designed to work together: Advanced Order Management, Advanced production Control, Advanced Warehouse Management, Essentials, Agent Integration Platform, Product Search and optional add-on Advanced Finance.

This is an inward-facing technical product role responsible for translating business requirements from the Product Manager into scalable, high-quality technical solutions across multiple products within a domain. This position ensures product architecture, delivery, releases, and cross-product dependencies are aligned and effectively coordinated.

You will safeguardthe functional andtechnical feasibility, integrity, and qualityofthe product scope, while supportingdomain-level alignment and enablingthe product development team to deliver against thestrategic product roadmap.

Key responsibilities

Define Product Architecture 

  • Partner with the Product Manager to understand the product vision, strategy, customer and market needs, and roadmap.
  • Contribute to the product vision and roadmap based on deep functional and technical expertise, product feedback, and emerging technology insights.
  • Document functional and technical requirements, solution designs, architectural principles, and technical decisions.
  • Validate technical feasibility, performance impact, scalability, and product integrity together with the lead developer.
  • Align technical design with user experience, persona-based user stories, business requirements, and the overall product strategy.
  • Ensure desired features are designed as part of a cohesive, scalable, and functional product.
  • Work with the product team to apply Studio’s newly defined AI technology, processes, and ways of working

Oversee Product Development & Support 

  • Own and manage the product backlog, translating prioritised roadmap initiatives into epics and actionable work items.
  • Work with development teams to design, build, test, and release products against the prioritised backlog and defined architecture.
  • Facilitate development team ceremonies, support delivery cadence, and track progress against agreed work items and release schedules.
  • Ensure the development team has a clear understanding of objectives, customer-driven requirements, and expected outcomes.
  • Coordinate the product development lifecycle to ensuretimelydelivery and high-quality implementation.
  • Manage implementation quality, testing outcomes, documentation, release notes, and complex Level 4 support topics.

Align Cross-Product Architecture (Lead)

  • Maintain an overview of all products within the domain and ensure architectural consistency across patterns, integrations, and technical decisions.
  • Identify cross-product dependencies, assess the impact of new features, and mitigate architectural risks across the domain.

Coordinate Domain Releases (Lead)

  • Coordinate domain-level release planning, aligning scope, dependencies, timelines, and release practices across products.
  • Support predictable delivery by proactively identifying and resolving cross-product risks and blockers.

Facilitate Product Architect Alignment (Lead)

  • Facilitate alignment among the team’s Product Architects, clarify ownership and responsibilities, and support decision-making on complex topics.
  • Act as a trusted sparring partner for complex functional and technical matters across the domain.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent

jobs.title: Senior Director, Platform Prioritization & Delivery
jobs.excerpt: Mission Lane is combining the power of data, technology, and exceptional service to pave a clear way forward for millions of people on the path to financial success.
jobs.description:
Mission Lane is combining the power of data, technology, and exceptional service to pave a clear way forward for millions of people on the path to financial success. By attracting top talent and leveraging cutting-edge technology, we’re enabling people to unlock real financial progress. Sound like a mission you can get behind?

We're looking for a Senior Director to own cross-functional prioritization and delivery across Mission Lane, reporting to the SVP, Product, Platform, & Delivery

The impact you'll make:

Every initiative Mission Lane ships – a better payment plan, a faster credit decision, a clearer way to see progress -- moves a customer forward. None of it ships in a vacuum. It depends on the right team picking it up at the right time, with the capacity to see it through, without adversely affecting another initiative.

The system that sorts through those prioritization decisions is yours to run. You’ll manage the framework and facilitate the discussions that decide what goes first when domains are moving at different speeds and carrying different risks. You'll often be bringing a room full of different perspectives to a shared answer.

This function is new at Mission Lane, and the framework for it is only partly in place. You're the one who fills in what's missing and runs it day to day, building the credibility that earns trust and adherence.

What you'll own:

  • A team of four Delivery Managers, each embedded in a different focus area (Collections, Data & AI/Model Process, Portfolio Management, and Acquisitions), including their coaching, growth, and workload balance
  • The prioritization tracker as Mission Lane's single source of truth for what's in flight, at what stage, and why, kept accurate enough that leaders trust it without double-checking
  • Weekly prioritization meetings, MBRs, and QBRs, run with enough rigor to hold up under executive scrutiny
  • Company-wide delivery standards, frameworks, and tooling that initiative teams actually adopt in their day-to-day work
  • Cross-functional alignment across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Credit, Marketing, Finance, and Legal/Compliance, clearing blockers and resolving trade-offs before they stall delivery
  • Post-initiative retrospectives that produce concrete changes to how the next initiative gets planned and delivered

You'll thrive in this role if:

  • You've led delivery inside an organization with genuine cross-functional complexity, spanning multiple teams and stakeholder groups.
  • You've built a prioritization or delivery process yourself, and can explain the tradeoffs in it clearly enough that someone new to it can follow the logic.
  • Your background is in product, program, or technical delivery leadership, with the credibility to work as a peer with engineering leads and data scientists.
  • You build just enough process to protect capacity and speed, no more.
  • You have direct conversations with senior stakeholders when priorities conflict, and you know how to bring a room to a decision.

Minimum qualifications:

  • A proven track record of building processes and oversight to drive improved speed to impact across an organization.
  • A proven track record leading and developing a team focused on organizational effectiveness which could include Delivery Managers, Program Managers, or similarly scoped delivery leaders
  • Experience working in a highly regulated and technical environment, with demonstrated ability to shape functional strategy and operate with a high degree of autonomy
  • Experience owning enterprise-level portfolio intake, prioritization, and execution tracking end to end, at a company operating at meaningful scale and complexity
  • A demonstrated ability to align senior and executive stakeholders across functions such as Product, Engineering, Finance, Credit, and Legal around shared priorities without relying on direct authority
  • Deep working knowledge of modern delivery methodologies and the judgment to adapt them to an organization's actual stage of maturity as well as rapidly changing technology
  • Experience structuring and running core enterprise operating cadences, such as weekly prioritization meetings, MBRs, and QBRs, that senior leadership relies on for accurate decision-making
  • Hands-on experience with modern portfolio and workflow tooling (e.g., Jira, Jira Align, Asana, Monday.com, Smartsheet), including evaluating and administering these tools at an organizational level
  • A background that includes hiring, coaching, and developing direct reports
  • Ability to travel ~4+ times per year for high quality in person collaboration

Preferred qualifications:

  • Direct experience in consumer lending, credit cards, or another regulated financial services environment, with working knowledge of compliance, credit risk, and legal considerations that shape delivery timelines
  • Experience scaling delivery governance and team structures inside a fast-growing, mid-sized organization moving through a similar stage of process maturity
  • Expertise configuring enterprise-grade portfolio tools (e.g., Jira Align, Dragonboat, Productboard) to connect strategic goals directly to team execution
  • Experience building portfolio dashboards (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) to track delivery velocity, resource utilization, and realized business impact

Compensation:

Annual full-time starting base salary range: $196,000 - $243,000

This role is eligible for additional compensation in the forms of participation in our annual incentive and equity programs.

Pay is based on factors such as work experience, education, certification(s), training, skills, and competencies related to the role. Mission Lane also offers a comprehensive benefits plan, which includes paid time off, 401(k) match, a monthly wellness stipend, health/dental/vision insurance options, disability coverage, paid parental leave, flexible spending account (for childcare and healthcare), life insurance, and a remote-first work environment.

About Mission Lane:

Founded in December 2018, Mission Lane is a purpose-driven fintech company based in the U.S., with headquarters in Richmond, Virginia.

It all started with a realization: nearly fifty percent of the adult population in the U.S. doesn’t have access to a clear line of credit. Most traditional credit card companies either overlook or overcharge this group because they have less-than-perfect credit scores or no scores at all. We decided this just wouldn’t do.

In partnership with our sponsor banks, we offer credit cards under the Mission Lane brand name, with better, clearer terms, and a more refined customer experience than the alternatives available to people working hard to improve their credit. To date, over four million consumers have chosen Mission Lane, earning high customer ratings on Credit Karma for its market segment and industry leading Net Promoter scores.

Mission Lane has cumulatively raised over $600 million of equity from leading investors, including Invus Opportunities, QED Investors, LL Funds, funds affiliated with Oaktree Capital Management, and other leading investors.

Our commitment to a workplace built on respect and dignity is guided by our core value of Unity. We believe that everyone plays a vital role in our shared purpose, and we actively cultivate an environment where all individuals have the opportunity to do their best work. By fostering a culture of empathy and collaboration, we create a strong sense of belonging and support for every team member.

Mission Lane is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or any other protected status.

Mission Lane provides reasonable accommodations to applicants who need them for medical or religious reasons, as required by law. Applicants can initiate an accommodation request by contacting .

Mission Lane is not sponsoring new applicant employment authorization and please, no third-party recruiters.

The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. Ehvert Mission Critical, a business unit within Salas O’Brien, is seeking an experienced 4D Construction Project Scheduler for a long-term independent contractor basis.

You will provide services as an independent, self-employed professional under a formal independent contractor agreement.

Role Summary:

We are seeking a skilled 4D Construction Project Scheduler as an independent contract worker to support the design and coordination of cutting-edge data center projects across the U.S. In this role, you will be responsible for modeling, designing power distribution, security and life systems, standby generators and UPS systems, performing calculations, preparing technical documentation, and ensuring design accuracy using advanced BIM and electrical engineering tools. You will collaborate closely with other disciplines in a dynamic, fast-paced environment, contributing to the full project lifecycle from schematic design through execution.   • Supportive dynamic environment
  • English classes made available.

  • Using estimating tools to calculate material quantities and labor requirements for project execution.
  • Creating Work Breakdown Structures (WBS), define tasks, allocate resources, and establish activity codes to clarify project scopes.
  • Calculating critical path, resource needs, and project slack to ensure timely delivery and resource optimization.
  • Generating GANNTcharts, resource allocation charts, and other essential reports for project stakeholders.
  • Collaborating with BIM teams to integrate project schedules with the Revit BIM model, facilitating the creation of 4D BIM schedules and construction simulations.

Qualifications & Experience:

  • A bachelor’s or master’s degree in engineering or construction
  • Written and spoken English B1 and higher
  • 5-10 years of experience in the construction industry managing complex construction projects with a large electrical and/or mechanical component; projects can be a variation of commercial, industrial, transportation, utilities.
  • Experience with Primavera P6, Microsoft Project required
  • Strong experience in Revit is a must
  • MS Access experience is an asset
  • Microsoft Office proficiency (Word, Excel, Outlook)
  • Strong organizational and management skills with the ability to multi-task and to initiate tasks
  • Attention to detail and problem-solving skills
    Self-starters that are ambitious and thrive in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to communicate technical knowledge in a clear and understandable manner
  • Excellent communication skills

Why Us?

  • Perform on high-profile, hyperscale, and AI data center projects in a rapidly expanding industry
  • Collaborate with leading professionals and global clients such as Microsoft, Oracle, Uber, and Amazon
  • Competitive terms of the contract
  • Dynamic environment fostering creativity through exposure to advanced technologies such as BIM, VDC, digital twins, and augmented reality

Collaborate with Ehvert Mission Critical, a business unit within Salas O’Brien, and help us achieve our international engineering goals!

Ehvert Mission Critical specializes in the design and construction management of data centers. We are a business unit within Salas O’Brien - a 4,000-person engineering and professional services firm, widely recognized for its extensive expertise and impressive project portfolio. With more than 10,000 projects annually and 100 offices across North America, Salas O'Brien is ranked #39 on Engineering News-Record’s 2024 Top 500 Design Firms list.

Ehvert Mission Critical, a business unit within Salas O’Brien, is an industry leader in data center facility engineering, specializing in hyperscale and AI data centers, designing massive data centers for global tech giants like Microsoft, Uber, Oracle, and Amazon. Our projects involve complex electrical, mechanical, automation, and security systems necessary to power, cool, and secure these high-demand facilities, often exceeding loads of 100 MW per facility and up to 500 MW per site.

We are recognized for our advanced engineering and construction techniques, including Building Information Modeling (BIM), Virtual Design and Construction (VDC), and augmented reality.

You will not be eligible for any employee benefits, and we will not withhold taxes, provide insurance(s), or make contributions to social security/pensions on your behalf. You are responsible for complying with all tax and labor obligations in your country of residence. About Us:

The way people buy software is changing. We’re creating what comes next.

Consensus is the world’s most trusted demo platform for B2B sales and marketing teams, rated #1 in Demo Automation on G2. We’re rethinking the demo experience from the first interaction to the live conversation.

Consensus connects every demo experience, from interactive product tours and videos to AI demo agents and live demos with real-time data, into one continuous buying experience. Every interaction creates demo intelligence that helps teams understand what buyers explored, what they cared about, and what they need next. The result? More context, less friction, faster sales cycles, higher conversions, and more capacity for sales and presales teams.

At Consensus, we’re not just another SaaS company. We’re a dynamic team on a mission to change how buyers buy. Your unique perspective isn’t just welcomed; it’s essential. We want people who bring curiosity, challenge the status quo, and are excited to have a real hand in shaping what comes next.

Our values aren’t just words on a wall. They show up in how we work, how we collaborate, and how we make decisions. We want you to show up ready to contribute and grow. Perfection isn’t the goal. It’s about putting your name on a version one, learning from it, and making it better.

If you’re ready to roll up your sleeves and help shape the future of B2B buying, we want you on our team.

Want to see Consensus in action for yourself? Check out ourdemo (in the Consensus platform—meta, right?)

About the Role:

Let's be clear about what this role is not: it's not a calendar babysitter, and it's not a job for someone arriving with a 2015 EA playbook. This is the operating system for our revenue leadership.

Our CRO's time is split between customers, prospects, the sales team, and the board, and it changes by the hour. You'll be the person who makes that work. You'll manage the CRO's email, calendar, travel, and priorities. You'll also run the rhythms that keep our revenue org aligned: forecast calls, pipeline reviews, QBRs, and Sales Kickoff. When a strategic deal needs executive time on short notice, you'll find the time and make sure the CRO walks in prepared.

And here's the part we mean most: we want someone AI-forward. Not "I've heard of ChatGPT" forward, but someone who looks at a workflow, asks "why are we doing it this way," and rebuilds it. We're an AI-forward company, and this role should show what that looks like in revenue operations.

What You’ll Do:

  • Run the CRO's rhythm. Manage email, calendar, and travel with judgment, not just logistics. You'll triage, prioritize, and protect time for the moments that move revenue: customer meetings, late-stage deals, and coaching the team.
  • Prep for every customer and prospect meeting. Before each executive meeting, pull the account context from the CRM, recent activity, and the account team's notes, and put it into a short brief the CRO can read in two minutes.
  • Own the revenue operating cadence. Schedule and coordinate the weekly forecast calls, pipeline reviews, sales leadership meetings, and quarterly business reviews. Track action items and follow up until they're closed.
  • Produce the big moments. Lead logistics and planning for Sales events. Support the CRO at conferences and customer events.
  • Support board and exec reporting. Help assemble the revenue sections of board decks and leadership updates. Set timelines, chase inputs from sales leaders, and make sure nothing arrives the night before.
  • See around corners. Spot the end-of-quarter crunch before it hits, flag the travel conflict before it happens, and prep the CRO before they know they need it.
  • Upgrade our workflows. Bring AI tools and automation into everything above.

What We’re Looking For:

  • Experience: 2+ years supporting senior executives (C-suite strongly preferred), ideally in a fast-moving SaaS or tech environment. Board meeting experience is a big plus.
  • Agility + precision: You move fast and you don't drop details. Most people are one or the other; we need both.
  • AI-forward, playbook-skeptical: You actively use AI tools in your work today. Tell us about a workflow you've automated or rebuilt—bonus points if AI was involved. We'd rather hear about your version one than your credentials.
  • Forward and backward thinking: You instinctively work backwards from deadlines and forwards from patterns. You're the person who says "in three weeks this is going to be a problem" in week one.
  • Discretion: You'll be trusted with board materials, compensation information, and conversations that can't leave the room. That trust is the foundation of this role.
  • Communication: Clear, warm, and concise in writing—you'll be drafting comms that go to the whole company.

Join Consensus and enjoy a robust benefits package designed with your well-being in mind:

  • Health & Wellness: Benefit from a generous employer contribution towards health insurance, with a variety of plans that include dental and vision coverage. Enjoy employer contributions to your HSA, and take advantage of HSA/FSA programs to maximize your tax savings.
  • Retirement Ready: Secure your future with our 401(k) plan featuring company-matching contributions.
  • Family First: We offer paid parental leave, so you can prioritize what matters most—your family.
  • Work-Life Balance: Enjoy unlimited PTO and 12 company holidays to recharge and refresh. Celebrate your birthday with a day off, and enjoy Flex Fridays, where every third Friday of the month is yours to unwind.
  • Flexible Work Options: Work in a flexible, remote environment that suits your lifestyle, with a top-tier WFH setup provided when you join.
  • Grow with Us: Participate in our professional development program to expand your skills and advance your career.
  • Give Back: Make a difference in your community with two paid volunteer days each year at a charity of your choice.

jobs.excerpt: Business Unit:Cubic Transportation SystemsCompany Details:When you join Cubic, you become part of a company that creates and delivers technology solutions in transportation to make people’s lives easier by simplifying their daily journeys, and defense capabilities to help promote mission success and safety for those who serve their nation.
jobs.description:
Business Unit:

Cubic Transportation Systems

Company Details:

When you join Cubic, you become part of a company that creates and delivers technology solutions in transportation to make people’s lives easier by simplifying their daily journeys, and defense capabilities to help promote mission success and safety for those who serve their nation. Led by our talented teams around the world, Cubic is committed to solving global issues through innovation and service to our customers and partners.

We have a top-tier portfolio of businesses, including Cubic Transportation Systems (CTS) and Cubic Defense (CD). Explore more on Cubic.com.

Job Details:

Position Summary

The Regional Head of Customer Success (RHCS) is the senior customer-facing leadership role for Global Services within a defined geographic region. The role carries end-to-end accountability for customer outcomes across all four Lines of Service; Contact Center (Customer Experience Centers), Technology & Service Operations, Financial Services, and Field Services, spanning both active deployment programs and steady-state service operations.

The RHCS operates as the single point of regional accountability for service governance, escalation management, and customer satisfaction, ensuring that Service Delivery Managers (SDMs), Technical Account Managers, Business Analysts, and Release Management & Planning resources are aligned, coordinated, and executing to Global Services standards. While SDMs retain program-level accountability, the RHCS provides the regional leadership layer that drives consistency, escalation resolution, and continuous improvement across the portfolio.

The role operates in a matrix environment. Multiple SDMs carry a dotted-line relationship to the RHCS, as do Release Management & Planning resources, Business Analysts, and Technical Account Managers embedded across programs in the region. The RHCS provides direction, prioritization alignment, and performance oversight across these resources without replacing the direct-line reporting structure of each function.

This role reports directly to the Senior Director, Customer Success and serves as the primary escalation and leadership interface between the regional program portfolio and the Global Services executive team.

Key Responsibilities

  • Regional Customer Success Leadership – Serve as the senior customer success leader for the region, accountable for the quality, consistency, and outcome of all customer-facing service activity across deployment and operations. The RHCS sets the standard for customer engagement across all four Lines of Service, drives a customer-first culture across SDMs and dotted-line functions, and ensures that every program in the region reflects Global Services delivery standards.
  • Deployment & Program Delivery Oversight – During active deployment phases, including program change, BAU change, security change, and maintenance activities, ensures that all Lines of Service are mobilized, coordinated, and executing to contracted scope and schedule. Coordinate readiness activities across Contact Center, Technology & Service Operations, Field Services, and Financial Services ahead of major go-lives and change events. Ensure SDMs are embedded and effective across all active deployment programs within the region and that customers receive proactive, high-quality engagement throughout the deployment lifecycle.
  • Service Operations & BAU Performance – In steady-state operations, ensure that contracted SLAs and KPIs are consistently met or exceeded across all programs and Lines of Service within the region. Maintain regional oversight of service performance, incident management, ticket resolution, and escalation handling. Ensure SDMs are driving operational discipline, meeting response and resolution targets, and managing customer satisfaction proactively. Provide consolidated regional performance visibility to the Senior Director, Customer Success, including risk flags, trend analysis, and improvement initiatives.
  • Escalation Ownership & Management – Own regional escalation management across all programs, ensuring timely resolution of high-severity incidents and complex service failures. Act as the primary escalation point of contact for SDMs across programs within the region. Support SDMs in managing escalations and ensuring clear ownership and rapid resolution pathways. Coordinate cross-functional responses across technical, operational, and service teams. Engage customers directly on critical incidents where issues exceed SDM scope. Align SDMs, Technology & Service Operations leadership, and functional teams to resolve complex, cross-program, or systemic issues. Ensure escalation closure with documented root-cause analysis and corrective actions. Provide timely visibility and structured updates to leadership on all high-priority issues. Reduce the escalation burden on the Senior Director, Customer Success and CSO by owning regional resolution pathways end-to-end. Drive consistent escalation handling practices across the region.
  • Cross-Line-of-Service Coordination – Coordinate service delivery across all four Lines of Service to ensure seamless, integrated customer outcomes. Resolve cross-functional dependencies, manage service handoffs, and ensure that no program or customer falls through the gaps between service functions. Lateral engagement with Contact Center, Technology & Service Operations, Field Services, and Financial Services leadership is a core and ongoing requirement of this role.
  • SDM Performance & Capability – Provide direction, coaching, and performance oversight to SDMs with a dotted-line relationship to this role. Ensure SDMs implement best practices in service governance, customer engagement, and escalation handling. Monitor SDM performance against regional standards and intervene where gaps are identified. Drive capability development across the SDM population in the region, reinforcing consistent application of Global Services frameworks.
  • Matrix Resource Coordination – Coordinate the activities of dotted-line resources, including SDMs, Business Analysts, Release Management & Planning functions, and Technical Account Managers, across programs in the region. Ensure these resources are prioritized effectively, operating to common standards, and contributing to regional customer outcomes in a coordinated manner. Navigate the matrix structure to remove blockers and align effort across functions.
  • Standardization & Continuous Improvement – Reinforce standardized governance cadence, reporting structures, KPI frameworks, and service improvement methodologies across all programs within the region. Identify best practices from individual programs and drive replication across the regional portfolio. Continuous improvement is approached not only at the program level but at the regional services model level.

Key Performance Metrics

  • Escalation Resolution Time – Time to resolve high-severity incidents from point of escalation to closure, tracked per priority tier across all programs in the region.
  • Client Satisfaction (CSAT / NPS) – Aggregated customer satisfaction and net promoter scores across all programs in the regional portfolio.
  • SLA & KPI Compliance Rate – Percentage availability, percentage response within SLA, resolution times, and percentage abatements across Non-Field and Field Services, covering Contact Center, Technology & Service Operations, and Field Services.
  • Incident Resolution Effectiveness – Reduction in repeat incidents and mean time to resolution versus baseline, tracking improvement across all Lines of Service within the region over time.
  • Unclosed Ticket Volume – Count of open and aged tickets across Contact Center, Technology & Service Operations, and Field Services per program within the region.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline
  • 12+ years of experience in service delivery, managed services, or mission-critical operations
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-program service portfolios in a matrixed environment
  • Proven track record of owning senior customer escalations and driving resolution across cross-functional teams
  • Strong ITIL-based service management expertise with practical application in live operational environments
  • Solid financial and commercial acumen, including cost-to-serve awareness and margin contribution understanding
  • Experience in transit, transportation systems, fare payments, or regulated technology environments
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and influence without direct authority across dotted-line and matrix reporting structures
  • Experience leading global or multi-region services in a matrixed organization
  • Exposure to PCI DSS, ISO 27001, or similar compliance and security frameworks

‎

Cubic Pay Range:

$190,000.00 - $210,000.00* + benefits.

‎ ‎

*Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several US geographic markets. The base pay for this position ranges from our lowest geographic market up to our highest geographic market.

The Cubic pay range for this job level is a general guideline only and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, applicable bargaining agreement (if any), or other law.

The Associate Director, Planning (AMD) serves as an essential strategic and operational lead within a planning pod. In this role, you bridge high-level strategy and flawless execution, leading the development of integrated media recommendations while managing day-to-day client relationships.

You are responsible for translating strategic direction into actionable, audience-first plans that tightly align media placement with creative messaging. Operating with a blend of analytical rigor and creative problem-solving, you coach and manage junior planning talent, elevate team output, and ensure operational and financial discipline across assigned accounts.

The Kind of Leader Who Thrives Here

  • Curious and Analytical: You are always asking "Why?" You dig beyond surface-level data to find meaningful insights and category white space.
  • A Strategic Storyteller: You distill complex inputs into clear, compelling narratives. You articulate a crisp media POV in both internal and external rooms with confidence.

Strategic Planning & Integration

  • Identify category white space and craft unique media moments that amplify creative impact and go beyond standard media placements.
  • Evaluate campaign performance against objectives, providing strategic POVs on optimizations and marketplace trends.
  • Develop strategic analyses (geographic, target audience, competitive audits) to guide plan direction and client spend recommendations.

Client Leadership & Collaboration

  • Own day-to-day client relationships, serving as a key point of contact and driving weekly status, recommendations, and campaign reviews.
  • Partner seamlessly across cross-functional agency teams—including Client Experience, Strategy, Creative, Activation, Analytics, CRM, and Finance—to deliver integrated output.
  • Represent a strong, clear media POV in key client presentations and internal strategic discussions.
  • Build and maintain productive, professional relationships with media vendor partners to stay ahead of marketplace innovation.

Team Leadership & Pod Operations

  • Manage, mentor, and coach junior pod members (Supervisors, Senior Planners, Planners), fostering their growth in planning craft, tool usage, and soft skills.
  • Master the art of delegation—balancing oversight with direct support to ensure flawless delivery while building bench strength.

Financial Stewardship & Growth

  • Identify organic growth opportunities across Media, Data & Analytics, and CRM, partnering with leadership to bring value-add ideas to clients.
  • Translates data and insights into clear, creative, and actionable media strategies.
  • Builds trust and strong alignment with clients and internal cross-functional leads.
  • Effectively delegates and develops junior planners into strong, autonomous strategists.
  • Maintains absolute precision in media math, flowcharts, and financial stewardship.
  • Proactively brings solutions and media POVs to the table rather than just identifying issues.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
  • 5-8 years of media planning experience within an agency setting.
  • Proven experience developing integrated plans across traditional and digital channels.
  • Demonstrated experience direct-managing or mentoring junior planning team members.
  • High proficiency in industry planning and research tools (e.g., MRI-Simmons, Resonate, YouGov, Vivvix, Pathmatics, SQAD, Guideline/MediaTools, Nielsen).
  • Strong media math acumen, financial discipline, and analytical problem-solving skills.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with a track record of effective client presentation.
