jobs.excerpt: It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!
jobs.description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

Job Description Summary:

The Senior Enterprise Engagement Manager owns delivery of assigned mainframe modernization engagements end to end — from assessment and delivery planning through migration, cutover, stabilization and handover — in environments where an unplanned outage is not an acceptable outcome. This role reports to the Director, Technical Project Management within Enterprise Services.

This is a senior individual contributor role on Rocket's Technical Career Path. You will run your engagements with a high degree of independence under limited to general supervision, exercising the judgement that keeps scope, schedule, cost, quality and risk under control, and escalating early — with a recommendation — when a decision needs the Director or an executive sponsor. The problems you take on are complex but generally well framed: they call for disciplined analysis across multiple systems, contracts and stakeholders rather than invention from a blank sheet.
You will also help raise the standard of the practice. That means coaching and reviewing the work of less experienced project managers on shared engagements, and contributing the templates, checklists and lessons learned that the Director is institutionalizing across Enterprise Services. The role has no direct reports — influence here comes from credibility with customers, delivery teams and peers.

Success looks like engagements that land on scope, schedule and margin; customers who treat you as a trusted delivery lead rather than a status reporter; and a project management practice that is measurably more repeatable because of what you contributed back to it.

Own assigned engagements end to end

  • Plan, organize and execute mainframe modernization software delivery and implementation engagements for assigned customers, from initiation through closeout, with a high degree of autonomy.
  • Hold accountability for scope, schedule, budget, quality and risk objectives on your engagements, which may span multiple concurrent workstreams, for example:
  • Assessment, discovery and delivery planning
  • Migration, re-platforming or re-hosting execution
  • Integration with surrounding systems and hybrid cloud targets
  • Testing, cutover and rollback readiness
  • Post-go-live stabilization, handover and customer adoption
  • Apply advanced project management and technical principles to delivery problems that are complex but mostly defined, weighing system, contractual and stakeholder considerations before committing to a course of action.
  • Set and continually manage delivery expectations with project team members, customer stakeholders and external partners.
  • Demonstrate a working understanding of software and hardware implementation activities — deployment, integration and customer adoption — sufficient to challenge plans, estimates and readiness claims credibly.

Control schedule, cost, change and risk

  • Develop, maintain and actively manage detailed project schedules, resource forecasts and cost performance throughout the engagement lifecycle.
  • Run change control: assess impact, guide customers and internal teams through the decision, and ensure changes are clearly documented, approved and communicated.
  • Maintain risk and issue registers with named owners, mitigations and follow-through, giving early visibility of anything that threatens a committed date or cost position.
  • Maintain requirement compliance matrices and governance artifacts so contractual obligations and delivery commitments are tracked and evidenced — particularly in regulated environments where change control and rollback planning are contractual.

Communicate, report and escalate

  • Facilitate regular project status meetings with customers, communicating progress, risks, dependencies and next steps in terms both technical and business stakeholders can act on.
  • Serve as the day-to-day point of accountability for your engagements, identifying risks and dependencies early and leading resolution.
  • Produce delivery-ready reporting, issue logs, action item registers, requirements documentation and customer presentations.
  • Support executive-level steering meetings led by the Director or an executive sponsor, supplying the delivery narrative, data and options those forums need.
  • Contribute to incident and problem management on your engagements, ensuring clear communication and root cause follow-up.

Strengthen the delivery practice

  • Provide guidance, coaching and review of work produced by less experienced project managers on shared engagements.
  • Contribute to the development, improvement and standardization of project management processes, tools, templates and best practices across Enterprise Services.
  • Lead or contribute to project postmortems and implementation reviews, converting lessons learned into changes other delivery teams can reuse.
  • Work cross-functionally with service delivery, Finance, Legal and GTM counterparts on the commercial and contractual mechanics of your engagements.

Qualifications

Required

  • 8+ years of relevant experience delivering technology projects, including vendor-side or consulting delivery to external customers.
  • Demonstrated ownership of engagements end to end — initiation through closeout — with personal accountability for scope, schedule, cost and quality.
  • Experience delivering software implementation or systems integration work in complex, production-critical customer environments.
  • Experience delivering under both Fixed Price and Time & Materials commercial models, and understanding of the delivery discipline each requires.
  • Strong stakeholder facilitation, written reporting and customer communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently under limited to general supervision, exercising judgement on complex delivery problems and escalating with a recommendation rather than a question.
  • University degree or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred

  • PMP, PRINCE2 or equivalent certification, or actively working toward certification.
  • Direct experience with mainframe modernization — IBM Z or IBM Power environments, migration or re-platforming programs, or hybrid cloud integration.
  • Delivery experience in regulated industries where auditability, change control and rollback planning are contractual requirements.
  • Experience coaching or mentoring project managers, or reviewing their delivery artifacts.
  • Experience contributing to delivery methodology, templates or PMO tooling — improving the practice, not only working within it.

Job Summary:

This job establishes overall business or technical strategy for risk management, influences executive-level decision-making through strategic risk assessments, partners with stakeholders to implement risk reduction strategies, monitors risk exposure, and leads initiatives for long-term sustainability and resilience.

Job Description:

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Establish overall business or technical strategy for risk management with significant impact on operations.
  • Influence executive-level decision-making through strategic risk assessments and recommendations.
  • Partner with stakeholders to implement strategies that reduce or transfer identified risks.
  • Monitor and analyze risk exposure to ensure alignment with organizational objectives.
  • Lead initiatives that contribute to long-term sustainability and resilience in the face of uncertainty.

Expected Qualifications:

  • 10+ years relevant experience and a Bachelor’s degree OR Any equivalent combination of education and experience.

Additional Responsibilities & Preferred Qualifications:

Role Summary:

PayPal is establishing a de novo industrial bank charter (ILC) and is seeking an experienced Chief Compliance Officer (“CCO”) to design, stand up, and lead the bank’s Compliance Management System (CMS). The CCO will be the primary compliance executive for the ILC, with independent access to the Board (or Board Risk & Compliance Committee) and day‑to‑day partnership with the CRO and senior leadership. The CCO will be responsible for developing and administering the Bank’s second line compliance management program to ensure adherence to applicable federal and state banking laws, regulations, and regulatory expectations. The CCO will report to the ILC’s Chief Risk Officer (“CRO”) and will have a direct line of communication to the Board’s Risk & Compliance Committee.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop, implement, and maintain the Bank’s Compliance Management System (“CMS”), ensuring alignment with regulatory guidance and Board-approved risk appetite and policies.
  • Oversee and maintain compliance policies and procedures designed to ensure that the Bank’s activities are conducted in accordance with applicable consumer protection, privacy, and regulatory laws and regulations.
  • Monitor changes in laws and regulations affecting the Bank and communicate the impact of such changes to management and the Board, recommending appropriate policy or procedural updates.
  • Oversee compliance testing and monitoring programs to identify control gaps or process weaknesses and track remediation activities through completion.
  • Serve as the primary liaison with regulatory agencies for compliance-related inquiries and examinations.
  • Collaborate with business lines and the first line of defense to ensure compliance risk is identified, assessed, and mitigated within acceptable tolerance levels.
  • Provide compliance training programs to ensure management and employees understand their responsibilities under applicable laws and regulations.
  • Work closely with the Bank’s CRA Officer to ensure that the Bank meets its community reinvestment obligations consistent with Board policy and applicable regulations.
  • Partner with the CRO to ensure enterprise-wide risk management processes appropriately incorporate compliance risk.
  • Report regularly to the CRO, senior management, and the Board’s Risk & Compliance Committee on the status of the Bank’s compliance posture, including significant findings, corrective actions, and emerging risks.
  • Effectively communicate and address regulatory inquiry or examination activities.
  • Establish and maintain effective communication and coordination with management and staff across all lines of business.
  • Participate in and capably make presentations and address questions at various management and Board-level committee meetings.

De Novo Charter Formation & ILC Buildout:

  • Lead the compliance workstream for the ILC de novo application, including program narratives, policies, risk assessments, governance charters, training plans, monitoring/testing strategies, and compliance components of the three-year business plan.
  • Translate conditions of approval from state and FDIC orders into actionable controls, milestones, and Board reporting.
  • Establish the bank’s second line CMS across governance, regulatory change, policies/procedures, training, monitoring & testing, complaint management, issues management, and independent audit coordination.
  • Embed compliance in product, servicing, marketing, operations, technology, and vendor onboarding. before first customer.
  • Stand up frameworks for BSA/AML/OFAC (in partnership with/overseeing the BSA Officer), UDAAP, fair banking/fair lending, third-party/fintech partnerships, privacy & data protection, records & reporting, and model/algorithm oversight (credit, fraud, and marketing use cases).

Ongoing Program Leadership (Post Opening):

  • Own the enterprise compliance risk assessment, risk appetite metrics (KRIs/KPIs), and the annual compliance plan; update dynamically as products, volumes, and partners scale.
  • Maintain and continuously improve policies covering federal and state banking and consumer protection laws/regulations (e.g., GLBA privacy & safeguards, FCRA, ECOA/Reg B, TILA/Reg Z, EFTA/Reg E, Reg` DD, Reg CC, Fair Lending, HMDA/CRA as applicable, UDAAP/UDAP, advertising/marketing, esign/edisclosures).
  • Oversee Compliance related aspects for deposits, lending (consumer and/or commercial, as applicable), payments, card issuance/network rules, ACH/NACHA, and digital channels (web/mobile).
  • Build and lead a high‑performing team covering Advisory, Monitoring & Testing, Regulatory Change, Complaints, Marketing/UD(A)AP Review, and Partner/Vendor Compliance; select and manage outside counsel/consultants as needed.
  • Implement and optimize a GRC/RegTech stack for regulatory change tracking, control testing, issues management, workflowed marketing reviews, and regulatory reporting.
  • Develop and oversee the bank’s Fair Lending review (qualitative & quantitative) program of bank models. Ensure marketing, loan offers, and loan approvals are made in line with ECOA guidance to protect individuals from discrimination, bias or disparate impact.
  • Create concise, risk‑based Board and executive reporting; chair/coordinate the Management Compliance Committee.

Regulator Engagement & Exams:

  • Serve as the primary compliance contact for the FDIC and the state banking department, coordinate with other agencies as applicable.
  • Lead examinations end‑to‑end: readiness, first‑day letters, on‑site/virtual exam management, corrective action plans, and sustainable remediation of MRAs/MRIAs/observations.
  • Maintain a forward‑looking regulatory change management process, brief leadership and the Board on developments and operational impacts.

BSA/AML/OFAC & Fraud Collaboration:

  • Oversee the design and adequacy of the BSA/AML/OFAC program (risk assessment, policies, CDD/KYC/EDD, transaction monitoring, SAR/CTR reporting, sanctions screening), partnering closely with the BSA Officer and Fraud/Risk leads.
  • Ensure governance over models/rules used in transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, credit, and fraud (thresholds, tuning, back‑testing, and independent validation, as applicable).

Third‑Party & Fintech/Partnership Oversight:

  • Establish and enforce Develop and oversee third‑party risk/compliance standards across vendors, program managers, fintech partners, and loan/deposit agents—covering due diligence, contracting, ongoing monitoring, complaints/issues, marketing/UD(A)AP controls, data use, and termination/exit.
  • Ensure clear bank level ownership of compliance obligations in partner programs; implement robust SLAs, testing, and reporting.

Culture, Training & Change Leadership:

  • Drive a strong “tone from the top” culture focused on customers and regulators.
  • Deliver targeted, role based compliance training for Board, executives, and staff; certify completion and effectiveness.
  • Embed compliance early in product/engineering lifecycles through formal product approval and marketing review processes.

Governance & Reporting Lines:

  • Primary reporting: ILC Chief Risk Officer
  • Direct line of communication: Board’s Risk & Compliance Committee; regular executive sessions with independent directors as appropriate.
  • Risk partnership: Close collaboration and regular reporting to the CRO on compliance risk profile, KRIs/KPIs, significant findings, corrective actions, and emerging risks.
  • Independence from revenue generating functions, with authority to escalate issues and pause or veto launches/marketing that present unacceptable compliance risk.

Required Qualifications:

  • 15+ years of progressive compliance leadership in U.S. depository institutions.
  • Demonstrated success building or materially upgrading a bank compliance program; de novo chartering experience strongly preferred.
  • Proven leadership of FDIC and state examinations and sustainable remediation of findings.
  • Expert knowledge of core banking and consumer protection laws/regulations, UDAAP, and third‑party/partnership compliance expectations.
  • Experience overseeing/partnering with BSA/AML/OFAC and Fraud functions.
  • Strong governance and Board reporting capability; mastery of compliance risk assessment, monitoring/testing, complaint management, and regulatory change management.
  • Track record recruiting, developing, and leading high caliber compliance teams in scaling environments.
  • Excellent executive communication and stakeholder management.
  • Bachelor’s degree required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • CRCM and/or CAMS; JD or related advanced degree a plus.
  • Experience with industrial loan companies and the parent/affiliate dynamics unique to ILC ownership.
  • Background in digital banking, bank‑as‑a‑service/fintech partnerships, or card/payments programs.
  • Hands on experience with GRC/RegTech platforms and data driven reporting.
  • Familiarity with privacy and data governance (GLBA, data minimization/retention, vendor data controls) and coordination with InfoSec on safeguards.

jobs.title: Automation QA Engineer (Lead)
jobs.excerpt: Bug Squisher Wanted: You’re an expert at making sure websites, storefronts, and backend systems work smoothly before they go live.
jobs.description:
Bug Squisher Wanted: You’re an expert at making sure websites, storefronts, and backend systems work smoothly before they go live. But you don’t just catch bugs. You build the systems that catch bugs before anyone else ever sees them. You can spot flaky tests from a mile away. Your test architecture is clean, scalable, and easy for other developers to follow. And when it comes to troubleshooting, you’re relentless — in the best possible way.

If this sounds like you, and you’re excited about a workday that’s fun, collaborative, technical, and full of purpose, let’s chat!

AlgaeCal is on the lookout for a Lead QA Developer to bring their skills to our lively QA team and help transform lives, one stable release at a time.

Small print here ⇒ We’re an eCommerce company. So, we want you to have eCommerce experience. Lots of it. You’ll be helping us improve the quality, stability, and reliability of our React-based storefront and internal middleware. So if automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, and digital marketing technology don’t light at least a small fire in your belly, you probably shouldn’t read any further.

Still here? Okay then…

This job will give you ALL the feels:

At AlgaeCal, we’re driven by a single idea. To end the fear of bone loss. In the United States, an estimated 54 million people have low bone density.

The good news? AlgaeCal has the world’s only clinically-backed natural solution to this problem. We give hope to everyone worried about bone loss. If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than at AlgaeCal.

You’ll love it here:

  • You’ll be working with a great team. The developers at AlgaeCal have been there, done that, and got the t-shirt. They’ve written more code than Alan Turing. They’ve learned more programming languages than C3PO. They’ve immersed themselves in so many development tasks that they’ve had to be pulled out of the Matrix by their ankles on a Friday evening. And the best part? They’re friendly, funny, and easy to work with.
  • You’ll use your powers for good. This isn’t one of those jobs that crush your soul with mindless tasks. On the contrary! You’ll help build the quality engineering systems that let us ship better storefront experiences, stronger middleware, and more reliable eCommerce platforms — all so we can spread a powerful message: bone loss is beatable.
  • You won’t be micromanaged. We’ll give you a clear set of KPIs, meaningful ownership, and crystal clear expectations. You’ll know what success looks like: stronger automation frameworks, cleaner CI/CD integration, fewer flaky tests, better reporting, and fewer defects slipping through to production.
  • We don’t have mattresses at the office. Seriously Elon, what’s up with that?!? You’ll be relieved to know this isn’t one of those Silicon Valley gigs that expects you to work ridiculously long hours and frowns upon family time. We’re not like that! We enjoy our life, and we want you to enjoy yours too.

This job might be for you if you’ve got…

  • 5+ years of QA development experience, with real examples of automated testing strategies you’ve built, maintained, improved, or scaled.
  • 2+ years of leadership, mentorship, or coaching experience. You don’t need a giant ego or a fancy title. But you do need to know how to guide other QA developers, review their work, support their growth, and raise the technical standard of the team.
  • A strong command of JavaScript and TypeScript. You don’t need to speak in code at dinner parties, (in fact, please don’t), but you should be very comfortable writing, reviewing, and improving automated tests in a modern JS/TS environment.
  • Hands-on experience with automated testing frameworks like Cypress, Playwright, or similar tools. If you’ve ever made a flaky test suite faster, cleaner, and more reliable, we’d love to hear about it.
  • The know-how to architect, optimize, and scale automated testing frameworks across frontend storefronts and backend middleware. Around here, that means working across our Shopify Hydrogen storefront and middleware
  • Experience integrating automated tests into cloud-based CI/CD pipelines. You understand that automation is only useful if it gives developers fast, reliable feedback, and doesn’t randomly blow up the build because someone sneezed near the test runner.
  • A sharp eye for quality metrics. We’re talking automation coverage, pipeline stability, test execution runtimes, flaky test reduction, production defect leakage, and the kind of reporting that helps the whole team make better decisions.
  • Comfort with specialized QA spaces like API contract testing, performance profiling, load testing, and browser developer tool profiling. You don’t have to know everything. But you do need to be curious, technical, and willing to dig. We’d also be impressed if you’ve worked with Python, PHP, Figma, Storybook, or Jest.
  • Next level bug prevention skills. In fact, you’re so good at dealing with bugs you should probably be deployed on a mission to Klendathu.

Now, time to be honest: is this really you?

If you’re nodding your head and feeling that flutter of excitement, then we can’t wait to meet you.

Other Qualities You’ll Need

At AlgaeCal, we’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:

  • You’re humble — you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own
  • You’re hungry to learn more
  • You’re people smart — in the sense that you’re a great teammate

The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at AlgaeCal. So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that is a better fit for you.

What Will You Earn?

We believe in rewarding top talent. Let’s talk about salary once we’ve had the chance to get to know you better. Rest assured, we’re generous and offer above-market pay for the right person. If you bring the skills and experience, we’ll make sure the compensation reflects that.

You’ll also enjoy the following benefits:

  • A generous healthcare package
  • Monthly team events and activities
  • Flexible Stat Holidays with the option to bank days for later use
  • Casual dress code

And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave. Culture is everything to us. Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible. But we know how to have fun and reward ourselves too.

How To Apply

So, do you have what it takes to become the next member of team AlgaeCal?

Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer our successful applicant. So, to make sure our future Lead QA Developer is the real-deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive at AlgaeCal, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application:

If this sounds like a position for you, please respond to this advertisement with your resume and cover letter. Please, read carefully:

Write a cover letter addressing:

Why are you the best Lead QA Developer for this role? Give quantifiable examples of related achievements, especially around automation frameworks, CI/CD testing, defect reduction, flaky test reduction, QA metrics, or mentoring other QA developers.

1. Describe why you fit perfectly with our values. Read them here:

2. What's the toughest challenge you’ve ever overcome in your life? How did you overcome it?

3. What are the last three books you’ve read?

4. What do you do for fun?

5. Explain what you’re doing now for a job:

6. If you don’t have one, explain why.

7. If you have one, explain why you’re looking elsewhere.

Upload your cover letter and resume

Ensure that your cover letter and resume are saved and sent as one file.

Yes, our hiring process is challenging, but it’s our way of selecting the best — and your way of ensuring your AlgaeCal teammates are tops.

Click the “Apply Now” button on this page and upload your cover letter and resume.

Note: Please include your cover letter WITH your resume in one document. Applications without a cover letter will not be read!

We are looking to hire as soon as we find the right person, so act quickly, and you can also expect a prompt response.

jobs.excerpt: DescriptionCapsLock is a global IT marketing company that pioneers unique, scalable customer acquisition solutions for B2C clients.
jobs.description:
Description

CapsLock is a global IT marketing company that pioneers unique, scalable customer acquisition solutions for B2C clients. We solve complex sales challenges across a wide range of industries, primarily for large North American partners. By integrating our expertise in Digital Marketing, IT, Design, AI-driven analytics, proprietary MarTech, and sales consulting, we deliver powerful, data-informed customer acquisition solutions.

At CapsLock, people, technology, and forward-thinking innovation lie at the heart of everything we do. Our diverse, global team, fluent in over 10 languages, thrives on open collaboration and the exchange of new ideas, pushing boundaries to ensure our clients' success.

Role overview

The role of a Senior CRO Copywriter focuses on creating persuasive, conversion-driven copy with the primary goal of improving marketing performance and conversion rates. This involves developing compelling copy for landing pages, ads, video scripts, and other marketing assets that attract cold audiences and encourage them to take action.

The CRO Copywriter works closely with marketing, creative, and testing teams to develop and optimize messaging based on customer research, campaign performance, and A/B testing results. Key tasks include developing new copy and messaging angles, researching audiences and competitors, analyzing copy performance, and continuously testing and refining copy to improve conversion metrics.

Responsibilities

  • Create conversion-focused copy for cold-traffic campaigns across landing pages, paid ads, video scripts, advertorials, forms, CTAs, and other funnel assets.
  • Research products, customers, competitors, markets, and advertising trends to identify new messaging opportunities.
  • Develop compelling headlines, hooks, offers, value propositions, benefits, and creative angles, translating technical product features into clear customer-focused messaging.
  • Ensure advertising claims are accurate, supportable, and compliant with client and platform requirements.
  • Create meaningful copy variations for structured A/B testing, analyze performance, and continuously iterate based on results.
  • Identify successful copy concepts and adapt them across similar clients, products, and industries.
  • Contribute winning concepts, failed tests, research, and learnings to the company's copywriting knowledge base.
  • Collaborate in brainstorming sessions with Marketers, Designers, Video Editors, Media Buyers, and other team members.
  • Use AI tools in the copywriting workflow to improve research, ideation, analysis, and production efficiency.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in Direct Response Copywriting, Performance Copywriting, Advertising Copywriting, or a similar conversion-focused role.
  • Native-level English.
  • Strong understanding of direct-response principles, customer psychology, and conversion-focused writing.
  • Proven experience writing landing pages, paid advertising copy, and performance creative.
  • Strong ability to develop headlines, hooks, offers, CTAs, value propositions, and messaging angles.
  • Experience writing for cold audiences and customer acquisition campaigns.
  • Ability to quickly research and understand unfamiliar products, markets, and customer segments.
  • Ability to translate features and technical information into clear customer benefits.
  • Experience creating structured copy variations for A/B testing.
  • Comfortable reviewing marketing performance data and using results to improve copy.
  • Strong attention to detail, grammar, proofreading, and consistency.
  • Ability to manage multiple clients, niches, and projects simultaneously.
  • Experience using AI tools for research, copy development, analysis, and workflow optimization.

Soft skills

  • Curious to explore new tools, formats, and creative approaches.
  • Adaptability to shifting priorities and fast-paced team dynamics.
  • High execution speed without compromising quality.
  • Consistent on-time delivery and attention to deadlines.
  • Strong attention to detail, especially when adhering to compliance and brand guidelines.

本ポジションはWizcorpでの雇用期間中、日本国内に在住していただく必要があります。

Wizcorpでは、スタジオの成長を支えるプロジェクトマネージャーを募集しています。あなたのこれまでのご経歴、スキル、経験、そして問題解決能力に応じて、最適なポジションをご紹介させていただきます。私たちは、経験や熟練度と同じくらい、人間性とキャラクターを重視しています。

このポジションに向いている方 👨‍🦰👩‍🦳🧑‍🦲

組織力があり、複数の言語でプロフェッショナルに話し、書くことができる方。臨機応変に対応でき、プレッシャーの中でも冷静さを保てる方。マルチタスクをこなし、異なる言語で交わされる複数のメールスレッドをフォローしながら、同時に社内メッセンジャーアプリとクライアントのメッセンジャーアプリに目を配り、メンバーに割り当てられたタスクの進捗を追うことができる方。ゲーム全般に興味があり、特にゲームがどのように作られるかに関心をお持ちの方。

当てはまる方、ぜひご応募ください!

業務内容 🎮📆🕹️

1日の始まりは、メールを確認して担当プロジェクトの進展をフォローすることから始まります。その後、チームとミーティングを行い、進行中のタスクについて話し合い、計画と予測が最新の状態であることを確認します。特定のチームメンバーと個別に話し合い、課題やボトルネックを明確にする必要があるかもしれません。そして、チームがクライアント側の担当者と、先方が希望するコミュニケーションチャネルを通じて連絡を取るサポートをします。

役割と責任 🛠️🧪✨

  • パートナーやクライアントと、日本語と英語でプロフェッショナルかつタイムリーにコミュニケーションを取る

  • 冷静さを保つ。プロジェクトマネージャーは、オーケストラの指揮者のようなもの:仕事のトーンとペースを設定します。他のメンバーがどのように業務を遂行しているかを把握し、適切な労働環境の中で優れた成果を出し続けられるようにする必要があります

  • 作業スピードを向上させ、反復作業に費やす時間を削減するための新しいアイデアやプロセスを提案する

  • タスク管理:スケジュールに従って作業を割り当て、関連性のある明確なフィードバックを提供し、最新の開発状況に応じて優先度を更新する

  • 社内の世界中のメンバーおよび姉妹スタジオと自信を持ってコミュニケーションする

  • チームメンバーの作業を計画・スケジュールし、進捗をフォローアップし、遅延や障害がある場合は他のプロジェクトマネージャーやクライアントに通知する

  • ファイルを受け取り、これまでのチームメンバーが設定した基準に従って整理・共有する

応募プロセス 🈸⚙️😊

① 書類選考: すべての応募者の履歴書を2週間以内に審査します。プロフィールが要件に合致する場合、初回面接の日程をご連絡いたします。

② 面接: お人柄、情熱、スキル、そして私たちの仕事への関心を評価するため、3回の面接を実施します。また、私たちのビジョンや価値観を共有する時間も大切にしています。私たちがあなたを面接するのと同じように、あなたも私たちを面接していると考えているからです。

③ リファレンスチェック: あなたの経験や働き方をより深く理解するため、前職の雇用主または専門的な関係者にリファレンスチェックを実施します。

④ 内定: 最終面接後、2週間以内に最終決定を行い、採用となった場合は詳細な内定通知をお送りします。

入社プロセス 🈴🗼🌅

入社プロセスをできる限りスムーズで心配のないものにするよう努めています。

内定承諾後、労働契約書と就業規則をお送りします。

理想的には1ヶ月以内にご入社いただきたいと考えていますが、現在の就業状況に応じて調整可能です。

初日には、マネージャーがチームメンバーを紹介し、6ヶ月の試用期間中のレビュースケジュールを設定します。試用期間を無事に完了できるよう、必要なサポートをすべて提供します。

Wizcorpでは、共に成長します。

シニアスタッフがサポートとメンターシップを提供します。デジタル学習教材へのアクセスも可能で、マネージャーがキャリア目標に基づいたトレーニングカリキュラムの策定を支援します。

当社のキャリア理念については、こちらをご覧ください:

応募要件

🤹 スキルセット 🤹

  • 日本語および英語が流暢であること

  • 優れた組織力と既存プロセスに従う能力

  • すべてのアウトプットを品質チェックし、修正のための建設的なフィードバックを提供できる細部への注意力

  • チームの一員として働き、クリエイティブな議論に貢献する意欲

  • レビューや建設的なフィードバックから学ぶことに積極的

  • 優れた個人的な時間管理能力

  • リモートワークおよび独立して業務を遂行する能力

jobs.title: AI Solutions Engineer
jobs.excerpt: We believe in bold ideas, diverse perspectives, and the drive to transform knowledge into impact.
jobs.description:
We believe in bold ideas, diverse perspectives, and the drive to transform knowledge into impact. Here, your curiosity fuels progress, your voice shapes innovation, and your ambition helps redefine what’s possible within science and learning. We are a culture that obsesses over impact, challenges, and drives what’s next to power infinite possibilities for our customers, colleagues and society at large.

About the Role:

Wiley Research is building new AI-powered capabilities across its operations — but the gap between deploying enterprise AI tools and genuinely changing how the business works remains large. Closing that gap requires someone who can move between business problem and technical solution: a developer who understands what the business needs, knows how to build it, and can deliver working tools quickly enough to prove their value before momentum is lost.

The Engineer, Business Solutions is that person. Working within the Business Management & Strategic Programs team, this role designs, builds, and deploys AI-powered tools and workflow automations that address real operational problems identified by the BMSP team and its partners across Research. The focus is on practical impact: automations that reduce manual effort, AI-assisted tools that improve decision quality, integrations that connect systems that currently require human intermediation, and rapid prototypes that let business teams test new approaches before committing to them at scale.

This role operates at the core of the BMSP team's crew model — working in 90-day sprints alongside the Associate Directors and Project Manager to identify problems, build solutions, and release them to the business. The developer is the technical engine of that model: the person who takes a well-scoped problem from the team and turns it into a working tool in weeks, not quarters. Speed, pragmatism, and business empathy are as important here as technical skill.

The right candidate is a developer who is genuinely excited about the intersection of AI and business operations — someone who finds as much satisfaction in solving a workflow problem for a publishing team as in writing clean code. They are comfortable working with non-technical stakeholders, translating vague business needs into defined requirements, and explaining technical trade-offs in plain language. They bring strong hands-on experience with LLM APIs, automation platforms, and the Microsoft 365 ecosystem, and are energized by a team that moves fast and iterates constantly.

Responsibilities

1. AI Tool Development & Deployment

  • Design, build, and deploy AI-powered tools and workflow automations that address business problems identified by the BMSP team and Research leadership — delivering working solutions within the 90-day sprint cadence.
  • Develop integrations between Wiley's existing systems (SharePoint, Teams, CRM, publishing platforms) and AI capabilities — enabling automated data flows, intelligent document processing, and AI-assisted decision support.
  • Build rapid prototypes and minimum viable products that allow business teams to validate new approaches quickly, before full development investment is committed.
  • Ensure that deployed tools are reliable, well-documented, and maintainable — with clear handoff to operational teams who will sustain them beyond the sprint in which they were built.

2. Business Problem Analysis & Solution Design

  • Work closely with the Associate Directors and Project Manager to understand business problems, translate them into technical requirements, and design solutions that are both technically sound and practically adoptable.
  • Participate in sprint planning and retrospectives — contributing the technical perspective to problem scoping, effort estimation, and solution evaluation, and helping the team make informed decisions about what to build and what to defer.
  • Identify where automation and AI can reduce low-value manual effort across Research operations — proactively surfacing opportunities to the team and building the business case for development investment.
  • Evaluate and recommend AI tools, platforms, and third-party services that could accelerate BMSP's solution delivery — balancing capability, cost, security, and ease of integration with Wiley's enterprise environment.

3. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Delivery

  • Partner with teams across Research — Publishing Operations, AI & Data Analytics, Finance, and others — to understand their workflows, identify integration points, and build solutions that work within the constraints of their existing systems.
  • Coordinate with Wiley's Technology & Operations teams to ensure that BMSP-developed tools comply with enterprise security, data governance, and IT standards — navigating the approval and deployment process without losing development momentum.
  • Communicate technical concepts, trade-offs, and progress clearly to non-technical stakeholders — ensuring that business partners understand what is being built, what it will and will not do, and when it will be ready.

4. Learning, Documentation & Continuous Improvement

  • Stay current with the rapidly evolving AI tooling landscape — evaluating new models, frameworks, and platforms as they emerge and identifying those most relevant to Wiley Research's use cases.
  • Document solutions, architectures, and integration patterns clearly — building a technical knowledge base that supports future development and allows other team members to understand and maintain what has been built.
  • Contribute to the BMSP team's retrospective practice — capturing lessons from each sprint, identifying what accelerated or impeded delivery, and recommending adjustments to improve the team's development velocity over time.

Requirements

Mandatory

  • 3–6 years of software development experience, with increasing focus on AI and automation tooling in an enterprise environment.
  • Strong proficiency in dataflow programming or frameworks such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, Caffe, MXNet, or Cognitive Toolkit, and may develop scripts in Python, Java, C++, Go, or equivalent languages; experience building and deploying web-based tools, APIs, or automated workflows in a business context.
  • Hands-on experience with large language model APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, or equivalent) — including prompt engineering, RAG architectures, function calling, and agent frameworks.
  • Experience with automation and integration platforms (Microsoft Power Automate, n8n, Zapier, or equivalent) and comfort working within the Microsoft 365 ecosystem (SharePoint, Teams, Power Platform).
  • Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business problems into defined technical requirements and working solutions — without requiring a formal specification to get started.
  • Strong communication skills: able to explain technical concepts and trade-offs to non-technical audiences clearly and without condescension.
  • Comfort working in a fast-paced, iterative environment where requirements evolve and speed of delivery matters as much as technical elegance.

Preferred

  • Experience with vector databases, embeddings, and retrieval-augmented generation for enterprise knowledge management or search applications.
  • Familiarity with MLOps practices and tools (containerization, cloud deployment, monitoring) for maintaining AI tools in production.
  • Experience in publishing, media, information services, or a comparable content-driven industry — familiarity with editorial, content production, or rights management workflows is an advantage.
  • Experience with data visualization and dashboard tooling (Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent) to support analytics and reporting use cases.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline — or equivalent practical experience.

For more than 200 years, we've transformed knowledge into discoveries that shape the world. Today, our global team of innovators, creators, and experts is driving what's next in science, education, and publishing—creating impact that reaches everywhere.

We're not just observers of progress. We're the ones accelerating scientific breakthroughs, advancing learning, and sparking innovation that redefines entire fields and improves lives.


Here, your talent matters. Your ideas have room to grow. And your work creates breakthroughs that can change everything.

About Upserve, Inc.

Upserve is an established restaurant technology and payments platform entering a restart phase under private equity ownership. The company serves independent and multi-location full-service restaurants and operates across software, payments, and financial services.

Role Summary

Upserve is seeking a strategic and results-oriented Vice President of Marketing to lead the company's end-to-end marketing strategy and execution. The VP of Marketing will be responsible for accelerating customer acquisition, driving merchant engagement, strengthening the Upserve brand, and supporting revenue growth across our payments, restaurant technology, and financial services businesses, including Merchant Cash Advance (MCA).

This executive will lead a high-performing marketing organization spanning demand generation, product marketing, customer lifecycle marketing, digital marketing, brand, communications, and marketing operations. The ideal candidate combines strategic vision with operational excellence and has a proven track record of building scalable B2B SaaS, fintech, or payments marketing organizations.

Key Responsibilities

Marketing Strategy & Growth

  • Develop and execute a comprehensive marketing strategy aligned with Upserve's growth objectives.
  • Drive customer acquisition across payment processing, restaurant technology solutions, and embedded financial products.
  • Build integrated marketing programs that increase qualified pipeline, merchant acquisition, customer retention, and lifetime value.
  • Establish annual marketing plans, budgets, and measurable performance goals.

Demand Generation

  • Own marketing-generated pipeline and contribution to new customer acquisition.
  • Optimize multi-channel campaigns across digital, content, email, events, partnerships, referral programs, and field marketing.
  • Improve conversion rates throughout the marketing and sales funnel.
  • Partner closely with Sales to maximize lead quality, speed-to-lead, and revenue conversion.

Product Marketing

  • Lead product positioning, messaging, competitive intelligence, pricing support, and go-to-market strategies.
  • Launch new products and enhancements that drive merchant adoption and revenue growth.
  • Develop compelling value propositions for restaurants, hospitality businesses, and small business owners.

Customer Marketing & Retention

  • Create lifecycle marketing programs that increase onboarding success, product adoption, customer engagement, and retention.
  • Partner with Customer Success and Sales to improve Net Revenue Retention (NRR) and Gross Revenue Retention (GRR).
  • Develop campaigns supporting merchant expansion opportunities, including payments optimization and MCA renewals.

Brand & Communications

  • Strengthen Upserve's market positioning as a trusted partner for restaurant technology and commerce.
  • Oversee brand strategy, public relations, thought leadership, social media, content marketing, and customer advocacy.
  • Ensure consistent messaging across all customer touchpoints.

Marketing Analytics & Operations

  • Establish a data-driven marketing culture focused on measurable business outcomes.
  • Collaborate with RevOps to build executive dashboards tracking campaign performance, pipeline generation, CAC, marketing ROI, conversion rates, and customer acquisition efficiency.
  • Optimize marketing technology, automation platforms, CRM integration, attribution models, and lead management processes in conjunction with RevOps

Leadership

  • Recruit, develop, and lead a high-performing marketing organization.
  • Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, experimentation, and continuous improvement.
  • Collaborate closely with Product, Sales, Customer Success, Finance, and Executive Leadership to achieve company objectives.
  • Present marketing strategy, performance, and investment recommendations to executive leadership and the Board as needed.

Required Qualifications

  • 12+ years of progressive B2B marketing leadership experience.
  • 5+ years leading high-performing marketing teams at the director level or above.
  • Demonstrated success driving growth within SaaS, fintech, payments, restaurant technology, or financial services organizations.
  • Proven experience building demand generation programs that deliver measurable pipeline and revenue growth.
  • Strong expertise in digital marketing, lifecycle marketing, product marketing, marketing analytics, and CRM platforms.
  • Experience managing multi-million-dollar marketing budgets.
  • Exceptional leadership, communication, and executive presentation skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience serving SMB customers, particularly restaurants or hospitality businesses.
  • Experience marketing embedded finance, payment processing, lending, or merchant cash advance products.
  • MBA or equivalent advanced business experience.

jobs.excerpt: We're currently hiring for remote team members in the following states: DC, DE, GA, MA, MD, NC, NH, NJ, OH, PA, SC, UT, and VA.
jobs.description:
We're currently hiring for remote team members in the following states: DC, DE, GA, MA, MD, NC, NH, NJ, OH, PA, SC, UT, and VA.

We're AWeber, a remote-first company that helps small businesses around the world form meaningful connections with their customers and grow their businesses using our marketing communication software. We are fanatical about small businesses and we hope you are too!

At AWeber, agentic development is core to how we build. Our engineers spend most of their time designing solutions for agents to implement and reviewing agent-generated work for quality and correctness. On the QA team, you build the agents that do that work. As a QA Engineer II, you will spend far less time hand-writing test cases than you would elsewhere, and far more time building and improving the agents that generate our coverage, diagnose our failures, and watch our systems, then proving that what they produce can be trusted.

We deploy continuously, many times a day, across a platform that small businesses run their livelihoods on. That makes your judgment the thing that protects them. You own quality end to end: the test strategy, the automated coverage, the exploratory testing that finds what automation never will, real-time monitoring of live systems, and the call on whether something is ready to ship. Your mission is to make our quality signals trustworthy, so that a green build actually means something and the team can move fast on top of it. When you find a gap in the process, we expect you to fix it and tell people, not just file it.

On any given day, you could be found writing the test plan for a feature before a line of it exists, reviewing an agent-generated test suite and rejecting it because the assertions do not prove the behavior they claim to, exploring a new release by hand and finding the edge case nobody specified, tightening an agent's harness so it stops producing flaky waits, diagnosing why a pipeline job fails only in staging, or writing up the cause of a failure so the next person does not have to rediscover it.

You'll thrive as a QA Engineer II if you

  • Treat a passing test suite as a claim to be verified rather than a result to be trusted, especially when an agent wrote it.
  • Take a project from start to finish on your own, resolve what you can independently, and escalate early on what you cannot.
  • Are comfortable being the person who says a release is not ready, and can make that case with evidence instead of instinct.
  • Investigate root causes rather than just rerunning a test, and write down what you learned so it compounds for the team.
  • Get genuinely curious about how a system breaks, and go looking for the edge cases nobody wrote a ticket for.
  • Default to proactive communication and understanding the value that comes from working in the open.
  • See a broken process and fix it, then tell people it changed, instead of routing around it quietly.
  • Stay steady when several priorities compete and a release is in flight, and recover fast when something gets through.
  • Embrace emerging technology while staying skeptical enough to ask what it costs, how it fails, and how we would know.

Required skills and qualifications

  • 4+ years in QA or test automation in an Agile environment, including hands-on experience building test automation frameworks and not only writing scripts inside someone else's.
  • API testing with Python, using pytest, unittest, or a comparable framework.
  • UI testing with Cypress and TypeScript, including the discipline of stable selectors and reliable page objects.
  • Demonstrated use of AI development tools and coding assistants to produce, review, or maintain tests, and the judgment to evaluate what they generate rather than accept it.
  • Solid understanding of CI/CD pipelines, ideally GitHub Actions, with the ability to diagnose a failing job rather than just report it.
  • Exploratory testing skill: finding meaningful defects in a running product without a script to follow.
  • Experience with Docker and containerized environments, Git and modern version control workflows, and API tooling such as Postman or curl.
  • Working experience with AWS services in a testing or deployment context.
  • Ability to apply proven QA techniques including requirement traceability, boundary value analysis, and application stability and usability testing.
  • Strong written communication. You will document test plans, failures, and sign-offs for an audience that includes both engineers and agents.
  • Proven ability to work self-directed in a deadline-driven environment, and the willingness to help more junior QA engineers on testing platforms and procedures.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience building agents and not only using them: writing and iterating on prompts, wiring up tool use, and getting a multi-step agent loop to run reliably against a real system.
  • Experience evaluating agent or LLM output systematically, whether through eval harnesses, scoring rubrics, or regression detection.
  • Experience testing in a high-volume agentic or AI-assisted codebase, including the verification and review challenges that come with it.
  • Experience with real-time monitoring and observability tooling, and using production signals to find quality problems before customers report them.
  • Experience with Kubernetes, or testing services deployed across multiple environments with differing states.
  • Familiarity with performance, load, or security testing.
  • Experience in a remote-first, asynchronous engineering culture.
  • Background in one of our domains: email or marketing SaaS, web platforms, or backend services at scale.
  • Working knowledge of the Atlassian stack (Jira, Confluence).

AWeber Benefits

  • 100% Remote - we're not going back to the office and here's why.
  • Strong culture that supports flexibility, entrepreneurialism, and collaboration. Think we should be doing something different? Share your feedback! We’re looking for you to add your AWesomeness to our culture.
  • We have some other pretty cool benefits to make your life easier:
    • 100% Company Paid PPO medical, dental, vision insurance (spousal and domestic partner benefits available).
    • 4-7 weeks of paid time off and holidays (based on tenure).
    • 4 week paid sabbatical (based on tenure).
    • 401K retirement plan with 4% company match.
    • Company Profit Share.
    • Home office equipment and internet stipend.
    • Tuition reimbursement, conferences, and learning opportunities.
    • Gym Memberships Reimbursement.
    • Company Paid Short Term Disability Insurance.
    • Company Paid Life Insurance.
    • Additional Supplemental Benefits (Long Term Disability, Critical Illness, and Additional Life Insurance).

jobs.title: Roblox AI Fracker
jobs.excerpt: What Is Fracking? Fracking is our term for repeatedly attacking a problem until you find an idea good enough for us to implement.
jobs.description:
What Is Fracking?

Fracking is our term for repeatedly attacking a problem until you find an idea good enough for us to implement.

You are given a problem.

For example:

  • A game's thumbnail CTR is too low

  • Players are dropping out at a certain point

  • An icon is not communicating clearly enough

  • A progression system feels weak

  • A monetisation mechanic is underperforming

  • A feature technically works but players do not care about it

Your job is not to brainstorm once and give us five suggestions.

You keep going.

You research the problem. You use AI. You study competitors. You look at player behaviour. You challenge the assumptions behind the problem. You generate ideas, discard bad ones and generate more.

You keep fracking until you find something that makes us say:

"Yes. We should actually implement that."

That is a successful frack.

Every successful frack earns you a $500 bonus.

The idea does not need to ultimately succeed after implementation. Games are experiments and sometimes good hypotheses still fail.

What matters is that your thinking was strong enough for us to commit time and resources to implementing the idea.

Over time, the goal is for a Fracker to become increasingly accurate.

Not just better at generating ideas.

Better at identifying which ideas are actually worth doing.

The Role

Yes, we are hiring a Roblox AI Fracker.

This is not a Producer role. It is not a traditional Game Designer role. You are not being hired to manage people, organise tickets or spend your day in meetings.

You are being hired to think with AI.

We operate several large Roblox games and there are constantly hundreds of things that could potentially be improved.

CTR. Thumbnails. Icons. Retention. Monetisation. Progression. Features. UX. Game loops. Social mechanics. Discovery. Small interactions. Strange problems nobody has properly investigated yet.

There are effectively unlimited problems.

The limited resource is high-quality human attention.

Your job is to apply that attention continuously.

You will spend your day fracking problems across our games.

You will use AI heavily. You will research. You will generate ideas. You will challenge assumptions. You will learn how our Creative Director thinks and over time develop your own intuition for what will actually work.

Most ideas will go nowhere.

That is expected.

The goal is not to generate the largest number of ideas.

The goal is to generate accurate ideas that are good enough to implement.

When one of your ideas gets implemented, that is a successful frack.

Every successful frack earns a $500 bonus.

What You Will Actually Do

  • Receive specific problems from our live Roblox games

  • Investigate why those problems exist

  • Generate potential solutions using AI, research and your own judgement

  • Frack problems around CTR, thumbnails, icons, retention, monetisation, progression, UX, gameplay and other areas

  • Study competitors and wider Roblox platform behaviour

  • Generate significantly more ideas than we could realistically implement

  • Ruthlessly eliminate weak ideas

  • Keep attacking a problem when the obvious answers are bad

  • Present your strongest solutions clearly

  • Learn directly from our Creative Director's decision-making and intuition

  • Track which ideas are implemented

  • Study what happens after implementation

  • Improve your judgement based on actual outcomes

  • Eventually challenge our assumptions when your judgement becomes strong enough

  • Teach future Frackers once you have demonstrated consistently strong performance

A Simple Example

Imagine we tell you:

"This game's thumbnail CTR is not good enough."

A normal approach might be to create three new thumbnails.

A Fracker goes much further.

You might analyse successful thumbnails across Roblox. Investigate competing experiences. Examine character size, composition, facial expressions, colour contrast, text usage and visual hierarchy.

You might generate 50 concepts with AI.

Then reject 45 of them.

You might realise the thumbnail is not actually the core problem and that the game's positioning itself is unclear.

You might identify a completely different visual concept nobody internally considered.

You present the strongest option.

If we decide:

"Yes. Put that into production."

That is a successful frack.

You earn $500.

Then you move onto the next problem.

What Counts as a Successful Frack?

We deliberately keep the definition simple.

A frack is successful when:

You propose an idea and we decide to implement it.

That is the trigger for the bonus.

You do not need to wait months for perfect performance data before getting rewarded.

If we believe your idea is good enough to commit development, art or operational resources to it and we implement it, you have successfully fracked the problem.

Successful frack = $500 bonus.

Implementation does not guarantee that the idea ultimately succeeds.

Games are unpredictable.

An experiment can be sensible and still fail.

Your job is therefore not to magically predict the future.

Your job is to continuously produce ideas with a high enough expected value that we believe they are worth testing.

Over time, we expect your accuracy to improve.

A strong Fracker should eventually reach a point where their judgement carries significant weight because they have repeatedly demonstrated that their ideas are worth implementing.

Who We Want

You must be Roblox native.

That does not mean you need to be an elite Luau programmer.

It means you genuinely understand Roblox.

You understand the platform, players, culture and what makes Roblox games work.

You should instinctively understand concepts such as discovery, CTR, retention, progression, monetisation, social systems and why Roblox players behave differently from traditional PC or console audiences.

You might currently be a:

  • Roblox developer

  • Game designer

  • Product-minded Roblox creator

  • LiveOps designer

  • Roblox analyst

  • Growth-minded developer

  • Experienced Roblox creator

  • Extremely obsessive Roblox player who has also built things

  • Someone difficult to categorise who is unusually good at solving game problems

We care much more about how you think than your current job title.

You Will Probably Be Good at This If

  • You are extremely curious

  • You naturally attack problems from multiple directions

  • You can spend hours thinking about one seemingly tiny issue

  • You use AI as a thinking multiplier rather than a replacement for thinking

  • You understand Roblox deeply enough to recognise bad platform advice

  • You generate a lot of ideas but are ruthless about discarding weak ones

  • You care whether something actually works rather than whether it sounds clever

  • You are competitive

  • You like measurable output

  • You like the idea of earning directly from strong ideas

  • You actively want your judgement tested against reality

  • You can take direct feedback without becoming attached to your ideas

  • You are comfortable being wrong repeatedly

  • You become increasingly effective as you accumulate context

You Will Probably Hate This Job If

  • You need a clearly defined checklist every morning

  • You want somebody to tell you exactly how to solve each problem

  • You believe brainstorming itself is valuable regardless of output

  • You produce huge strategy decks instead of answers

  • You have never seriously used AI

  • You do not understand Roblox

  • You are uncomfortable having your ideas rejected constantly

  • You care more about owning an idea than finding the best solution

  • You prefer maintaining processes over solving problems

  • You want a role where performance is difficult to measure

How Compensation Works

You receive a base salary.

On top of that:

Every successful frack earns you $500.

The base salary exists because experimentation is inconsistent and we do not expect every idea to work.

The bonus exists because we want the incentive to remain extremely clear:

Find things worth doing.

There is no expectation that every problem produces a successful frack.

Some problems will take hours.

Some may take days.

Some will produce nothing useful.

Others may produce multiple ideas that we decide to implement.

The objective is not to optimise for cheap quantity.

It is to continuously improve your accuracy.

As the team grows, Frackers will learn from one another, compare approaches and continuously increase the accuracy of the group.

The long-term objective is for the combined judgement of the Fracking team to eventually exceed the intuition of the people currently making those decisions.

The Long-Term Idea

We are starting with Roblox.

But Fracking is ultimately a system for allocating more intelligent attention to problems.

One Fracker learns how we think.

Several Frackers learn from each other.

The strongest Frackers teach new ones.

The team develops institutional knowledge around which approaches work and which do not.

Eventually you have an entire group spending every working day attacking problems that otherwise would never receive enough attention.

The goal is not an enormous brainstorming department.

It is an accuracy department.

A human and AI problem-solving engine whose sole purpose is to continuously identify better decisions.

Think of it as bitcoin mining for hit-making.

Instead of mining hashes, you are mining for ideas worth implementing.

Every time you find one, you earn $500.

We call that Fracking.

How to Apply

Do not send us a generic cover letter explaining that you are passionate about games.

Tell us:

  1. Your Roblox experience

  2. Which Roblox games you understand particularly well and why

  3. The AI tools you currently use and how you use them

  4. One thing you believe a successful Roblox game is currently doing badly

  5. What you would change and why

If your answer to number four is interesting, we will probably have something to talk about.

Bausch + Lomb (NYSE/TSX: BLCO) is a leading global eye health company dedicated to protecting and enhancing the gift of sight for millions of people around the world—from the moment of birth through every phase of life. Our mission is simple, yet powerful: helping you see better, to live better.

Our comprehensive portfolio of over 400 products is fully integrated and built to serve our customers across the full spectrum of their eye health needs throughout their lives. Our iconic brand is built on the deep trust and loyalty of our customers established over our 170-year history. We have a significant global research, development, manufacturing and commercial footprint of approximately 13,000 employees and a presence in approximately 100 countries, extending our reach to billions of potential customers across the globe. We have long been associated with many of the most significant advances in eye health, and we believe we are well positioned to continue leading the advancement of eye health in the future.

This is an exciting time at Bausch + Lomb as we build our industry leading pharmaceutical and consumer pipeline. Over the course of the Company’s history, Bausch + Lomb has always stood at the forefront of cutting-edge scientific and technological optical advancements, and today, Bausch + Lomb is more focused than ever on developing and offering new treatments to meet unmet eye health needs. This role will enable our aspiration of the Bausch + Lomb mission of helping people see better to live better. This is an opportunity for a highly motivated translational scientist to be a key scientific contributor to building a best-in-class pharmaceutical and consumer pipeline.

Responsibilities:

Scientific role that contributes through translational nonclinical PK, PK/PD, ADME, clinical pharmacology and pharmacometrics in establishing Bausch + Lomb as the leader in eye health scientific innovation.

Technical Excellence

  • Leads clinical pharmacology, PK, PD, and pharmacometrics activities across multiple programs spanning the Rx ophthalmic pipeline (e.g., dry eye, glaucoma, retinal disease, ocular surface disease) and consumer eye health pipeline.
  • Contributes to action plans that best meet drug development business objectives, including candidate selection, first-in-human strategy, dose selection and justification, special population strategy, and life-cycle management.
  • Provides overall clinical pharmacology timelines and deliverables to inform portfolio prioritization and resourcing decisions.
  • Negotiates with other functional areas on project outcomes and deliverables to balance conflicting demands of time, cost, and quality/performance.
  • Contributes to development of departmental goals and influences strategic PK/PD decisions for the department.

Scientific and Technical Accountability

  • Evaluates technical and scientific aspects of projects, including ocular and systemic PK, ocular bioavailability and distribution, PK/PD modeling, exposure–response analysis, population PK, PBPK, and quantitative systems pharmacology where applicable.
  • Designs and oversees nonclinical PK, TK and clinical pharmacology studies, including first-in-human, ocular PK, drug–drug interaction, QT/QTc, hepatic/renal impairment, pediatric, and bioequivalence/bridging studies relevant to ophthalmic products.
  • Applies scientific expertise to interpret clinical and nonclinical data and clearly communicates implications to management, including go/no-go recommendations.
  • Maintains up-to-date knowledge of PK/PD data analysis, modeling and simulation methods and software (e.g., NONMEM, Monolix, Phoenix WinNonlin/NLME, R, Simcyp, GastroPlus, MATLAB).

Regulatory Strategy and Submissions

  • Reviews study protocols and reports including for regulatory filings and anticipates regulatory questions.
  • Leads authoring of pharmacokinetics and clinical pharmacology sections of regulatory documents including IND/CTA, IB, briefing packages, pre-IND/EOP2/pre-NDA meeting materials, NDA/BLA/MAA/505(b)(2), DMFs, and periodic safety updates.
  • Leads responses to health authority questions and represents Pharmacokinetics and Clinical Pharmacology in agency interactions.
  • Ensures alignment with ICH, FDA, EMA, and other applicable guidance for ophthalmic and systemic products.

Team Member Activities

  • Identifies issues and supports issue resolution; conducts risk assessments and helps develop contingency plans; assures projects remain aligned with strategic objectives.
  • Provides scientific and strategic consultation to R&D, Regulatory, and all levels of management on critical development decisions.
  • Identifies and develops process improvement initiatives and reviews recommendations with management for approval and sponsorship.
  • May conduct due diligence assessments for in-licensing, acquisition, and partnership opportunities; summarizes pharmacokinetic and clinical pharmacology findings and represents the function on due diligence teams.
  • Communicates and presents key pharmacokinetics and clinical pharmacology information and strategy to management, regulatory agencies, external peers, scientific advisory boards, and KOLs.

Requirements:

Education and Experience

  • PhD in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacometrics, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacology, Biomedical Engineering, or related discipline with typically 6+ years of relevant experience.
  • Experience with PK, PBPK, PK/PD, pharmacometrics or systems pharmacology, and/or drug metabolism and transporters. Ophthalmic drug development, topical/ocular PK, or ocular pharmacology experience is strongly preferred.

Technical and Functional Knowledge

  • Demonstrated leadership in PK/PD, biopharmaceutics, and pharmacometric activities from planning through implementation and completion across multiple projects.
  • Experience across a range of development phases (discovery support through Phase 3 and life-cycle management); experience with 505(b)(2), ANDA bridging, or OTC/consumer product pathways is advantageous given the Rx and Consumer pipeline.
  • Working knowledge of pharmaceutical drug development processes, ICH guidelines, and FDA/EMA clinical pharmacology expectations, including ophthalmic-specific guidance.
  • Proficiency with modeling and simulation tools (e.g., NONMEM, Phoenix WinNonlin/NLME, Monolix, R, Simcyp, GastroPlus).

Communication and Team Skills

  • Communicates openly and honestly with all colleagues.
  • Connects unrelated concepts and generates original or unique ideas.
  • Influences colleagues to achieve cross-functional alignment.
  • Manages conflict and difficult conversations in a constructive, transparent way.
  • Expert in industry best practices & trends with the ability to drive change.
  • Exceptional influencing, partnership, and collaboration skills to solve scientific and business problems and drive results.
  • Experience in the selection and oversight of vendors.
  • Knowledge of the cGMP practices and compliance requirements.
  • Excellent written, presentation, and verbal communication skills.

At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.

We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team:

Upstart's Core Pricing team drives key initiatives that directly influence our revenue streams, unit economics, and product strategy. The team builds and evolves the common systems used to translate underwriting insights into accurate risk and profitability decisions for every loan we originate, while enabling a seamless borrower experience across products.

As a Principal Software Engineer on Core Pricing, you will provide technical leadership that spans engineering, machine learning, and product organizations — not just the Pricing team. You will shape the long-term architecture, strategy, and operating model for pricing systems that serve multiple product lines and stakeholders across the company. Working in close partnership with engineering, ML, product, and business leaders across Personal Loans, Auto, HELOC, and adjacent platforms, you will lead the development of scalable, low-latency, highly reliable services that convert ML underwriting outputs into pricing decisions, and you will help define the future of Upstart's pricing platform as the company expands into new products, markets, and capabilities.

Our stack spans Python (Django, FastAPI, Celery), Kotlin/Spring Boot, gRPC/Protobuf, Temporal for workflow orchestration, AWS (S3, RDS/Postgres, ElastiCache), Kubernetes/Helm, and Datadog for observability.

How you'll make an impact

  • Define the cross-company technical vision and roadmap for Upstart's pricing platform, ensuring alignment across Pricing, Personal Loans, Auto, HELOC, ML, and Product organizations.
  • Lead the architectural evolution from tightly coupled, sequential workflows toward modular, reusable platform capabilities across loan products.
  • Design and improve Tier 0/Tier 1 services where latency, throughput, availability, and financial correctness are all critical.
  • Partner closely with machine-learning scientists and engineers to create reliable, scalable boundaries between models and production pricing systems.

  • Clarify service, API, configuration, and ownership boundaries across Pricing, Personal Loans, Auto, HELOC, and adjacent platform teams.
  • Evaluate runtime and language choices pragmatically, including where Python, Kotlin, Rust or Go best serve long-term system needs.
  • Reduce operational burden through better testing, observability, failure isolation, incident learning, and architecture that limits blast radius.
  • Lead company-wide technical discussions, surface trade-offs clearly, and build alignment across Engineering, ML, Product, Data, Security, Compliance, and business partners.
  • Stay close to implementation through design reviews, prototypes, and critical code while mentoring senior technical leaders and making the people around you more successful.
  • Prioritize technical-debt and platform investments based on business value, risk reduction, and long-term return rather than technical elegance alone.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field - or equivalent practical experience - plus 8 or more years of software engineering experience.
  • A track record of setting architecture and technical direction for large, complex distributed systems used across multiple teams or products.
  • Deep backend engineering experience and production proficiency in at least one of Python, Kotlin, or Java; willingness and ability to work effectively in a predominantly Python environment.
  • Experience designing or operating Tier 0/Tier 1 services with demanding latency, throughput, availability, and correctness requirements.
  • Strong understanding of APIs, service-oriented or modular architectures, containerization, cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS), and maintainable software design.
  • Hands-on technical judgment: you can move from strategy and architecture into concrete designs, prototypes, debugging, and critical implementation decisions.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to explain complex systems, constraints, and trade-offs to technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Demonstrated success leading cross-organization technical decisions — balancing the needs of engineering, machine learning, and product teams — and influencing without direct authority.
  • Experience mentoring senior engineers and expanding the effectiveness and scope of other technical leaders.
  • Strong product and business judgment, including the ability to balance delivery, reliability, technical debt, risk, and long-term investment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building calculation-heavy, real-time decisioning, pricing, marketplace, risk, fraud, payments, trading, auction, or advertising systems.
  • Experience partnering with machine-learning teams or productionizing models at scale, including clear boundaries between modeling workflows and production services.
  • Experience modernizing a mature or tightly coupled platform through staged migration while continuing to deliver customer and business value.
  • Experience with AWS, Kubernetes, microservices, event-driven systems, and production observability.
  • Additional production experience with Rust or another performance-oriented language.
  • Background or applied exposure in statistics, mathematics, economics, econometrics, financial systems, or other quantitative domains.
  • Experience in a rapidly scaling or changing organization where architecture had to evolve alongside the business.

Position location Remote

The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S but are encouraged to to still spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites. The in-person sessions’ cadence varies depending on the team and role; most teams meet once or twice per quarter for 2-4 consecutive days at a time.

Job Title

Senior Project Manager, TDS

Job Description Summary

The Senior Project Manager is accountable for the successful delivery of complex, high-risk, and high-visibility initiatives. This role operates with a high degree of autonomy and judgment, anticipating delivery risks and executive decision needs before escalation is required.

Senior Project Managers are trusted delivery leaders who engage confidently with sponsors, steering committees, and executives (VP and C-suite). They consistently translate complexity into clear options, guide executive decision-making, and model strong delivery and leadership behaviors across the PMO. Senior Project Managers maintain executive trust through transparent delivery health reporting, credible financial forecasts, and early identification of risks and trade-offs.

Job Description

Delivery Leadership

  • Lead end-to-end delivery of complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives across scope, schedule, budget, risk, and quality.
  • Anticipate delivery risks, dependencies, and constraints beyond what is explicitly documented.
  • Proactively identify and address issues before executive escalation is required.
  • Drive disciplined execution while adapting approaches based on project complexity and business context.
  • Own project financial management, including: Budget planning, Forecasting, Variance analysis and Identification of cost risks and trade-off options
  • Ensure formal project closeout, transition to operations, and lessons learned capture.

Governance & Decision Readiness

  • Operate with PMO standards and governance as baseline expectations.
  • Prepare executive-ready deliverables that anticipate leadership questions and decision friction.

  • Engage governance forums proactively rather than reactively.
  • Provide accurate financial insights and recommendations to support executive decision-making.
